bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: =漢紀五十四=

translations.literal: 【Han Records Fifty-Four】
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 54】

sentences.zh: 起柔兆困敦，盡著雍攝提格，凡三年。

translations.literal: Beginning from Rouzhao-Kundun through Zhuoyong-Shetige—in all, three years.
translations.idiomatic: Spanning the years from Rouzhao-Kundun through Zhuoyong-Shetige—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝丁

translations.literal: Emperor Xian (section Ding)
translations.idiomatic: Reign of Emperor Xian (section Ding)

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，癸酉，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day guiyou, there was a general amnesty and a change of reign era.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on guiyou day, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 2董承、張楊欲以天子還雒陽，楊奉、李樂不欲，由是諸將更相疑貳。

translations.literal: 2 Dong Cheng and Zhang Yang wished to return the Son of Heaven to Luoyang; Yang Feng and Li Yue did not wish it; because of this the generals became mutually suspicious and divided.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng and Zhang Yang wanted to bring the emperor back to Luoyang, but Yang Feng and Li Yue opposed the move, and the commanders grew mutually suspicious and disloyal.

sentences.zh: 二月，韓暹攻董承，承奔野王。

translations.literal: In the second month, Han Xian attacked Dong Cheng; Cheng fled to Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Han Xian attacked Dong Cheng, who fled to Yewang.

sentences.zh: 韓暹屯聞喜，胡才、楊奉之塢鄉。

translations.literal: Han Xian encamped at Wenxi; Hu Cai and Yang Feng at Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian encamped at Wenxi, while Hu Cai and Yang Feng held Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 胡才欲攻韓暹，上使人諭止之。

translations.literal: Hu Cai wished to attack Han Xian; the Emperor sent someone to instruct and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Cai prepared to attack Han Xian, the emperor sent envoys to order him to desist.

sentences.zh: 3汝南、潁川黃巾何儀等擁眾附袁術，曹操擊破之。

translations.literal: 3 The Yellow Turbans He Yi and others of Runan and Yingchuan gathered followers and attached themselves to Yuan Shu; Cao Cao attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He Yi and other Yellow Turban leaders in Runan and Yingchuan rallied their bands to Yuan Shu; Cao Cao defeated them in battle.

sentences.zh: 4張楊使董承先繕修雒陽宮。

translations.literal: 4 Zhang Yang had Dong Cheng first repair the palaces of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang sent Dong Cheng ahead to restore the palaces at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太僕趙岐為承說劉表，使遣兵詣雒陽，助修宮室；

translations.literal: The Grand Master of the Stables Zhao Qi persuaded Liu Biao on Cheng's behalf to send troops to Luoyang to help repair the palace buildings;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Master of the Stables Zhao Qi persuaded Liu Biao on Dong Cheng's behalf to dispatch troops to Luoyang to help repair the palaces;

sentences.zh: 軍資委輸，前後不絕。

translations.literal: military supplies were continuously forwarded, without interruption before and after.
translations.idiomatic: and military supplies flowed in without interruption.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，丙寅，帝遣使至楊奉、李樂、韓暹營，求送至雒陽，奉等從詔。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day bingyin, the Emperor sent envoys to the camps of Yang Feng, Li Yue, and Han Xian, requesting that they escort him to Luoyang; Feng and the others obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on bingyin day, the emperor sent envoys to the camps of Yang Feng, Li Yue, and Han Xian asking them to escort him to Luoyang, and they complied.

sentences.zh: 六月乙未，車駕幸聞喜。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei in the sixth month, the imperial carriage arrived at Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day in the sixth month, the imperial procession reached Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 5袁術攻劉備以爭徐州，備使司馬張飛守下邳，自將拒術於盱眙、淮陰，相持經月，更有勝負。

translations.literal: 5 Yuan Shu attacked Liu Bei to contend for Xuzhou; Bei had his Major Zhang Fei guard Xiapi while he personally led troops to resist Shu at Xuyi and Huaiyin; they faced off for a month, each side gaining victories in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu attacked Liu Bei to seize Xuzhou. Liu Bei left his major Zhang Fei to hold Xiapi while he personally led troops against Yuan Shu at Xuyi and Huaiyin; the two sides grappled for a month, each winning skirmishes in turn.

sentences.zh: 下邳相曹豹，陶謙故將也，與張飛相失，飛殺之，城中乖亂。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of Xiapi Cao Bao, a former officer of Tao Qian, had a falling-out with Zhang Fei; Fei killed him, and the city fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Bao, the chancellor of Xiapi and a former officer of Tao Qian, fell out with Zhang Fei, who killed him; the city was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 袁術與呂布書，勸令襲下邳，許助以軍糧。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu wrote to Lü Bu, urging him to strike Xiapi and promising to supply him with army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu wrote to Lü Bu urging him to strike Xiapi and promising military provisions.

sentences.zh: 布大喜，引軍水陸東下。

translations.literal: Bu was greatly pleased and led his army east by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was delighted and marched east by land and river.

sentences.zh: 備中郎將丹陽許耽開門迎之。

translations.literal: Bei's Central Gentleman of the Palace Danyang Xu Dan opened the gates to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dan of Danyang, a gentleman-attendant in Liu Bei's service, opened the gates to admit him.

sentences.zh: 張飛敗走，布虜備妻子及將吏家口。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei was defeated and fled; Bu captured Bei's wife and children and the families of his officers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei was routed and fled; Lü Bu seized Liu Bei's wife and children and the families of his officers.

sentences.zh: 備聞之，引還，比至下邳，兵潰。

translations.literal: When Bei heard of it he turned back; by the time he reached Xiapi his army had collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei heard the news he turned back, but his troops disintegrated before he could reach Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 備收餘兵東取廣陵，與袁術戰，又敗，屯於海西。

translations.literal: Bei gathered his remaining troops and marched east to take Guangling; he fought Yuan Shu and was defeated again, and encamped at Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei rallied his remnants and marched east against Guangling; he fought Yuan Shu again, was defeated once more, and encamped at Haixi.

sentences.zh: 飢餓困踧，吏士相食，從事東海麋竺以家財助軍。

translations.literal: Hunger and distress pressed upon them; officers and soldiers ate one another; the Attendant Clerk of Donghai Mi Zhu used his family wealth to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: Beset by hunger and desperation, his men resorted to cannibalism; Mi Zhu of Donghai, an attendant clerk in his service, supported the army with his family fortune.

sentences.zh: 備請降於布，布亦忿袁術運糧不繼，乃召備，復以為豫州刺史，與并勢擊術，使屯小沛。

translations.literal: Bei requested to surrender to Bu; Bu was also angry that Yuan Shu's grain shipments did not continue, and so summoned Bei, reappointed him Inspector of Yuzhou, joined forces with him to strike Shu, and had him encamp at Xiaopei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei offered to submit to Lü Bu, who was himself angry that Yuan Shu had failed to keep supplying grain; Lü Bu recalled Liu Bei, reappointed him Inspector of Yuzhou, allied with him against Yuan Shu, and stationed him at Xiaopei.

sentences.zh: 布自稱徐州牧。

translations.literal: Bu styled himself Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu declared himself Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 布將河內郝萌夜攻布，布科頭袒衣，走詣都督高順營。

translations.literal: Bu's general Hao Meng of Henei attacked Bu by night; Bu, with head bare and garments stripped, fled to the camp of the Commander Gao Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's general Hao Meng of Henei attacked him by night; Lü Bu fled bareheaded and half-dressed to the camp of his commander Gao Shun.

sentences.zh: 順即嚴兵入府討之，萌敗走；

translations.literal: Shun immediately marshaled troops and entered the headquarters to suppress him; Meng was defeated and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shun at once led disciplined troops into the headquarters to suppress the mutiny; Hao Meng was routed and fled;

sentences.zh: 比明，萌將曹性擊斬萌。

translations.literal: by dawn Meng's officer Cao Xing struck and beheaded Meng.
translations.idiomatic: and by dawn Hao Meng's officer Cao Xing struck and killed him.

sentences.zh: 6庚子，楊奉、韓暹奉帝東還，張楊以糧迎道路。

translations.literal: 6 On the day gengzi, Yang Feng and Han Xian escorted the Emperor eastward in his return; Zhang Yang met the road with grain.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day, Yang Feng and Han Xian escorted the emperor eastward; Zhang Yang supplied grain all along the route.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲子，車駕至雒陽，幸故中常侍趙忠宅。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiazi, the imperial carriage reached Luoyang and lodged at the former residence of the Regular Palace Attendant Zhao Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiazi day, the imperial procession reached Luoyang and took up residence in the former mansion of the eunuch Zhao Zhong.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛丑，幸南宮楊安殿。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinchou, the Emperor visited the Yang'an Hall of the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinchou day, the emperor moved into the Yang'an Hall of the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 張楊以為己功，故名其殿曰楊安。

translations.literal: Zhang Yang regarded it as his own achievement and therefore named the hall Yang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang, claiming credit for the restoration, had the hall named Yang'an after himself.

sentences.zh: 楊謂諸將曰：「天子當與天下共之，朝廷自有公卿大臣，楊當出扞外難。

translations.literal: Yang said to the generals: "The Son of Heaven should be shared with all under Heaven; the court has its own grand ministers and officials—Yang should go out to repel external dangers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang told the other commanders, "The Son of Heaven belongs to the empire; the court has its own ministers. I should go out and hold the frontier against outside threats.

sentences.zh: 」遂還野王。

translations.literal: " He thereupon returned to Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then withdrew to Yewang.

sentences.zh: 楊奉亦出屯梁，韓暹、董承並留宿衛。

translations.literal: Yang Feng also went out to encamp at Liang; Han Xian and Dong Cheng both remained as palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng likewise withdrew to encamp at Liang, while Han Xian and Dong Cheng stayed behind as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以安國將軍張楊為大司馬，楊奉為車騎將軍，韓暹為大將軍、領司隸校尉，皆假節鉞。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the Pacifying-the-State General Zhang Yang was appointed Grand Marshal, Yang Feng Chariots-and-Cavalry General, Han Xian Grand General and acting Colonel-Director of the Retainers; all were granted staffs of authority and axes.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day, Zhang Yang was made Grand Marshal, Yang Feng General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Han Xian Grand General with concurrent duties as Colonel-Director of the Retainers; each received the staff of authority and ceremonial axe.

sentences.zh: 是時，宮室燒盡，百官披荊棘，依牆壁間，州郡各擁強兵，委輸不至；

translations.literal: At this time the palace buildings had been burned to nothing; the hundred officials pushed through brambles and leaned against walls; each province and commandery held strong armies of its own, and forwarded supplies did not arrive;
translations.idiomatic: The palaces had been burned to ruins; officials picked their way through brambles and sheltered against broken walls; the provinces and commanderies each held their own armies, and no tribute reached the capital;

sentences.zh: 群僚飢乏，尚書郎以下自出採穭，或飢死牆壁間，或為兵士所殺。

translations.literal: the assembled ministers were hungry and destitute; those below the rank of Master of Writing went out themselves to gather grain stalks; some starved to death between the walls, others were killed by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: and the court was starving. Masters of writing and those below them went out to gather fallen grain; some died of hunger among the ruins, others were killed by soldiers.

sentences.zh: 7袁術以讖言「代漢者當塗高」，自云名字應之。

translations.literal: 7 Yuan Shu, because of a prophecy saying "He who replaces Han should be Tu-gao," said that his own name corresponded to it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu seized on the prophecy that "the one who will replace Han is Tu-gao" and claimed that his own name fulfilled it.

sentences.zh: 又以袁氏出陳，為舜後，以黃代赤，德運之次，遂有偕逆之謀。

translations.literal: He also held that the Yuan clan came forth from Chen, were descendants of Shun, and that yellow would replace red in the sequence of dynastic virtue; he thus formed a plan of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued that the Yuan clan sprang from Chen, were heirs of Shun, and that yellow—the color of earth—would succeed red in the cycle of dynastic virtue; on this basis he plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 聞孫堅得傳國璽，拘堅妻而奪之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Sun Jian had obtained the imperial transmission seal, he detained Jian's wife and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Sun Jian had obtained the imperial seal, he detained Sun Jian's wife and seized it from her.

sentences.zh: 乃聞天子敗於曹陽，乃會群下議稱尊號；

translations.literal: Then, hearing that the Son of Heaven had been defeated at Caoyang, he assembled his subordinates to discuss assuming an exalted title;
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the emperor had been defeated at Caoyang, he convened his officers to discuss proclaiming himself emperor;

sentences.zh: 眾莫敢對。

translations.literal: none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: but no one dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 主簿閻象進曰：「昔周自後稷至于文王，積德累功，參分天下有其二，猶服事殷。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yan Xiang advanced and said: "Formerly Zhou from Houji down to King Wen accumulated virtue and piled up merit, held two-thirds of all under Heaven, and still served Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Yan Xiang stepped forward and said, "From Houji down to King Wen, the house of Zhou accumulated merit for generations and held two-thirds of the realm, yet still served the Yin.

sentences.zh: 明公雖弈世克昌，未若有周之盛；

translations.literal: Your Excellency, though flourishing through successive generations, has not reached Zhou's greatness;
translations.idiomatic: Your lordship, though prosperous for generations, has not matched Zhou's grandeur;

sentences.zh: 漢室雖微，未若殷紂之暴也！

translations.literal: the House of Han, though enfeebled, is not like King Zhou of Yin's cruelty!
translations.idiomatic: and the house of Han, though weakened, is nothing like the tyranny of King Zhou of Yin!

sentences.zh: 」術默然。

translations.literal: " Shu was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Shu said nothing.

sentences.zh: 術聘處士張範，範不往，使其弟承謝之。

translations.literal: Shu invited the Recluse Zhang Fan; Fan did not go but had his younger brother Cheng decline on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu invited the scholar-recluse Zhang Fan, who refused to come and sent his younger brother Zhang Cheng to decline on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 術謂承曰：「孤以土地之廣，士民之眾，欲徼福齊桓，擬跡高祖，何如？

translations.literal: Shu said to Cheng: "I, with the breadth of my territory and the multitude of my people and soldiers, wish to seek the fortune of Duke Huan of Qi and model the footsteps of the High Ancestor—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu asked Zhang Cheng, "With my broad lands and numerous people, I mean to emulate Duke Huan of Qi and follow in the footsteps of the High Ancestor—what say you?

sentences.zh: 」承曰：「在德不在強。

translations.literal: " Cheng said: "It lies in virtue, not in strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng replied, "Success lies in virtue, not in brute strength.

sentences.zh: 夫用德以同天下之欲，雖由匹夫之資而興霸王之功，不足為難。

translations.literal: To use virtue to align with the desires of all under Heaven—even starting from the resources of a common man, to raise the achievement of hegemon and king is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: One who wins men's hearts through virtue can rise from humble origins to hegemonic greatness without difficulty.

sentences.zh: 若苟欲僭擬，干時而動，眾之所棄，誰能興之！

translations.literal: If one rashly wishes to usurp and act against the times, abandoned by the multitude—who could raise such a cause!
translations.idiomatic: But if you grasp at usurpation and move against the times, you will be abandoned by the people—who could then raise you up?

sentences.zh: 」術不悅。

translations.literal: " Shu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu was displeased.

sentences.zh: 孫策聞之，與術書曰：「成湯討桀稱『有夏多罪』，武王伐紂曰『殷有重罰』，此二主者，雖有聖德，假使時無失道之過，無由逼而取也。

translations.literal: Sun Ce, hearing of it, wrote to Shu: "Tang of Cheng attacked Jie under the banner 'Xia has many crimes'; Wu of Zhou attacked Zhou under the banner 'Yin has heavy punishments.' These two rulers, though possessing sage virtue, if the times had lacked the faults of losing the Way, would have had no means to press forward and seize power.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce heard of this, he wrote to Yuan Shu: "King Tang attacked Jie under the banner 'Xia is full of crimes'; King Wu attacked Zhou of Yin under the banner 'Yin is steeped in punishments.' Both were sages, yet neither could have overthrown his sovereign had the throne not already forfeited the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 今主上非有惡於天下，徒以幼小，脅於強臣，異於湯、武之時也。

translations.literal: The present sovereign is not evil toward all under Heaven but is merely young and coerced by powerful ministers—this differs from the times of Tang and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Our present sovereign has done no wrong to the realm; he is merely young and bullied by powerful ministers—a far cry from the age of Tang and Wu.

sentences.zh: 且董卓貪淫驕陵，志無紀極，至於廢主自興，亦猶未也，而天下同心疾之，況傚尤而甚焉者乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Dong Zhuo was greedy, licentious, arrogant, and overbearing, his will without limit or end; even when he went so far as to depose the sovereign and raise himself, he had not yet succeeded, yet all under Heaven united in hatred of him—how much more one who imitates his excesses and goes further!
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo was greedy, licentious, and insolent beyond measure; he deposed the emperor and set himself up, yet the empire united against him before he could succeed—how much worse will it be for one who copies his crimes and goes further still!

sentences.zh: 又聞幼主明智聰敏，有夙成之德，天下雖未被其恩，咸歸心焉。

translations.literal: I have also heard that the young sovereign is wise and keen, possessing virtue matured from of old; though all under Heaven has not yet received his grace, all turn their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: I hear moreover that the young emperor is intelligent and precociously gifted; though the realm has not yet felt his beneficence, all hearts already incline toward him.

sentences.zh: 使君五世相承，為漢宰輔，榮寵之盛，莫與為比，宜效忠守節，以報王室，則旦、奭之美，率土所望也。

translations.literal: Your lordship's family for five generations in succession has been chief minister to Han; the splendor of honor and favor has no equal—you should manifest loyalty and preserve integrity to repay the royal house; then the beauty of the Duke of Zhou and Duke Shi would be what all the land hopes for.
translations.idiomatic: Your house has served as chief ministers to Han for five generations; no family has known such honor. You should prove loyal and steadfast in repayment to the throne—the glory of the Duke of Zhou and Duke Shi is what the whole realm expects of you.

sentences.zh: 時人多惑圖緯之言，妄牽非類之文，苟以悅主為美，不顧成敗之計，古今所慎，可不孰慮！

translations.literal: Many in the time are deluded by the words of charts and wefts, recklessly dragging in texts of unrelated categories, deeming it beautiful merely to please the lord and not considering plans of success or failure—what ancients and moderns alike have cautioned against; can one not deliberate carefully!
translations.idiomatic: Too many men today are seduced by apocryphal prophecies, wrenching texts to fit their purpose and flattering their lord without weighing success or failure—a folly warned against in every age. Surely you will think this through carefully!

sentences.zh: 忠言逆耳，駁議致憎，苟有益於尊明，無所敢辭！

translations.literal: Loyal words offend the ear; refuting discourse provokes hatred; if it benefits your exalted clarity, I dare not decline to speak!
translations.idiomatic: Loyal counsel grates on the ear and frank debate breeds resentment, yet if it serves your high purpose I dare not hold my tongue!

sentences.zh: 」術始自以為有淮南之眾，料策必與己合，及得其書，愁沮發疾。

translations.literal: " Shu had at first thought himself possessed of the masses of Huainan and calculated that Ce would surely join with him; when he received the letter he was grieved and dejected and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu had counted on his Huainan armies and assumed Sun Ce would side with him; when the letter arrived he was stricken with grief and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 既不納其言，策遂與之絕。

translations.literal: Since he did not accept his words, Ce thereupon broke with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu rejected his advice, Sun Ce broke with him entirely.

sentences.zh: 8孫策將取會稽<ref>孫策將取會稽句原文此段繫於八月，在「曹操在許」於後。

translations.literal: 8 Sun Ce was about to take Kuaiji. [ref: The sentence "Sun Ce was about to take Kuaiji" in the original text was attached to the eighth month, after "Cao Cao was at Xu."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce prepared to seize Kuaiji. [Editor's note: In the original text this passage stood under the eighth month, after "Cao Cao was at Xu."

sentences.zh: 今移往「曹操在許」之前。

translations.literal: It is now moved to before "Cao Cao was at Xu."]
translations.idiomatic: It has been moved to precede "Cao Cao was at Xu."]

sentences.zh: </ref>，吳人嚴白虎等眾各萬餘人，處處屯聚，諸將欲先擊白虎等。

translations.literal: The Wu men Yan Baihu and others, each with more than ten thousand followers, were encamped everywhere; the generals wished first to strike Baihu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Baihu and other Wu bandit chiefs had more than ten thousand men each and were encamped throughout the region; Sun Ce's officers wanted to attack them first.

sentences.zh: 策曰：「白虎等群盜，非有大志，此成禽耳。

translations.literal: Ce said: "Baihu and the others are a pack of bandits without great ambition—they are prey ready to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce said, "Men like Baihu are mere bandits without grand ambitions—they can be captured at leisure.

sentences.zh: 」遂引兵渡浙江。

translations.literal: " He thereupon led his army across the Zhe River.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched his army across the Zhe River.

sentences.zh: 會稽功曹虞翻說太守王朗曰：「策善用兵，不如避之。

translations.literal: The Merit Officer of Kuaiji Yu Fan said to the Administrator Wang Lang: "Ce is skilled in using troops; it would be better to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan, merit officer of Kuaiji, urged the administrator Wang Lang, "Sun Ce is a formidable commander—you would do better to avoid a fight.

sentences.zh: 」朗不從。

translations.literal: " Lang did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang refused.

sentences.zh: 發兵拒策於固陵。

translations.literal: He raised troops to resist Ce at Guling.
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops and met Sun Ce at Guling.

sentences.zh: 策數渡水戰，不能克。

translations.literal: Ce repeatedly fought battles across the water but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce fought repeated battles across the river but could not break through.

sentences.zh: 策叔父靜說策曰：「朗負阻城守，難可猝拔。

translations.literal: Ce's uncle by marriage Sun Jing said to Ce: "Lang relies on natural barriers and holds the city in defense; it is hard to seize in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce's uncle Sun Jing advised him, "Wang Lang holds a fortified position behind natural barriers; you cannot storm it quickly.

sentences.zh: 查瀆南去此數十里，宜從彼據其內，所謂攻其無備，出其不意者也。

translations.literal: Chadu lies several tens of li south of here; you should from there seize the interior—what is called attacking where there is no defense and striking where it is unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Chadu lies a few dozen li to the south; you should seize it and strike from within—attack where he is unprepared and take him by surprise.

sentences.zh: 」策從之，夜，多然火為疑兵，分軍投查瀆道，襲高遷屯。

translations.literal: " Ce followed this plan; at night he lit many fires as a feint, divided his army and sent it along the Chadu road, and raided the encampment at Gaoqian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce agreed. That night he lit many fires as a diversion, split his force along the Chadu road, and stormed the camp at Gaoqian.

sentences.zh: 朗大驚，遣故丹陽太守周昕等帥兵逆戰，策破昕等，斬之。

translations.literal: Lang was greatly alarmed and sent the former Administrator of Danyang Zhou Xin and others to lead troops to meet the attack in battle; Ce defeated Xin and the others and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang was thrown into panic and sent the former Danyang administrator Zhou Xin and others to intercept him; Sun Ce routed and killed them.

sentences.zh: 朗遁去，虞翻追隨營護朗，浮海至東冶，策追擊，大破之，朗乃詣策降。

translations.literal: Lang fled; Yu Fan followed close behind, encamping to protect Lang, and crossed the sea to Dongye; Ce pursued, inflicted a great defeat, and Lang thereupon came to Ce to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang fled; Yu Fan followed close behind to protect him and sailed to Dongye; Sun Ce pursued, inflicted a crushing defeat, and Wang Lang came in person to surrender.

sentences.zh: 策自領會稽太守，覆命虞翻為功曹，待以交友之禮。

translations.literal: Ce himself took the post of Administrator of Kuaiji, reappointed Yu Fan as Merit Officer, and treated him with the courtesy due a friend.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce appointed himself Administrator of Kuaiji, reinstated Yu Fan as merit officer, and treated him as an intimate friend.

sentences.zh: 策好遊獵，翻諫曰：「明府喜輕出微行，從官不暇嚴，吏卒常苦之。

translations.literal: Ce was fond of roaming and hunting; Fan remonstrated: "Your lordship delights in going out lightly and traveling incognito; your attendants have no time to be strict, and the clerks and soldiers are constantly distressed by it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce loved to hunt; Yu Fan remonstrated, "Your lordship delights in slipping out incognito; your escort cannot keep proper order, and your officers and men suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 夫君人者不重則不威，故白龍魚服，困於豫且，白蛇自放，劉季害之。

translations.literal: A lord of men who is not weighty lacks authority; thus the white dragon in fish garb was trapped by Yu Qie, and the white serpent that released itself was harmed by Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who does not maintain his dignity lacks authority: the white dragon disguised as a fish was caught by the fisherman Yu Qie, and the white serpent that went abroad on its own was slain by Liu Bang.

sentences.zh: 願少留意！

translations.literal: I wish you would give a little heed!
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to take heed!

sentences.zh: 」策曰：「君言是也。

translations.literal: " Ce said: "Your words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 」然不能改。

translations.literal: " Yet he could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not break the habit.

sentences.zh: 9曹操在許，謀迎天子。

translations.literal: 9 Cao Cao was at Xu and planned to welcome the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was at Xu and planned to welcome the emperor to his base.

sentences.zh: 眾以為「山東未定，韓暹、楊奉，負功恣睢，未可猝制。

translations.literal: The multitude held that "the east of the mountains is not yet settled; Han Xian and Yang Feng, relying on their achievements, are arrogant and overbearing—it cannot be suddenly controlled.
translations.idiomatic: His advisers argued that "the east is still unsettled; Han Xian and Yang Feng are arrogant with their past service and cannot be subdued in haste.

sentences.zh: 」荀彧曰：「昔晉文公納周襄王而諸侯景從，漢高祖為義帝縞素而天下歸心。

translations.literal: " Xun Yu said: "Formerly Duke Wen of Jin received King Xiang of Zhou and the feudal lords followed like shadows; the High Ancestor of Han wore mourning white for the Emperor Yi and all under Heaven turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu replied, "Duke Wen of Jin received King Xiang of Zhou and the feudal lords flocked to him; the High Ancestor wore mourning for Emperor Yi and won the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 自天子蒙塵，將軍首唱義兵，徒以山東擾亂，未遑遠赴。

translations.literal: Since the Son of Heaven suffered dust on the road, the General was first to raise the righteous army, but only because the east of the mountains was in turmoil had he no leisure to go far in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the emperor fell into exile, you were first to raise the righteous banner, but turmoil in the east kept you from going to his aid.

sentences.zh: 今鑾駕旋軫，東京榛蕪，義士有存本之思，兆民懷感舊之哀。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage turns back its wheels; the Eastern Capital is overgrown with weeds; men of righteousness harbor thoughts of preserving the root; the myriad people cherish grief for the old.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial carriage is turning homeward, Luoyang lies in ruins, loyal men yearn to restore the dynasty, and the people mourn the capital they have lost.

sentences.zh: 誠因此時，奉主上以從人望，大順也；

translations.literal: Truly to take this moment, uphold the sovereign above to follow the people's hopes—this is the great accord;
translations.idiomatic: If you seize this moment to receive the emperor and satisfy the people's hopes, you will align with the greatest mandate;

sentences.zh: 秉至公以服天下，大略也；

translations.literal: to hold utmost fairness to bring all under Heaven to submission—this is the great strategy;
translations.idiomatic: hold yourself to utmost fairness and win the realm—that is the grand strategy;

sentences.zh: 扶弘義以致英俊，大德也。

translations.literal: to uphold expansive righteousness to draw men of excellence—this is the great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: and uphold righteous purpose to gather the talented—that is supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 四方雖有逆節，其何能為？

translations.literal: Though the four quarters have rebellious conduct, what can they accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: Rebels may stir in the provinces, but what can they achieve?

sentences.zh: 韓暹、楊奉，安足恤哉！

translations.literal: Han Xian and Yang Feng—how are they worth worrying over!
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian and Yang Feng are hardly worth your concern!

sentences.zh: 若不時定，使豪傑生心，後雖為慮，亦無及矣。

translations.literal: If you do not settle matters in timely fashion and let heroes and champions take heart, afterward even if you take thought, it will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If you delay, ambitious rivals will take heart; even if you reconsider later, it will be too late.

sentences.zh: 」操乃遣揚武中郎將曹洪將兵西迎天子，董承等據險拒之，洪不得進。

translations.literal: " Cao thereupon sent the General of the Martial Yang Cao Hong to lead troops west to welcome the Son of Heaven; Dong Cheng and others held strategic points and refused him, and Hong could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then sent General of the Martial Yang Cao Hong west with troops to welcome the emperor, but Dong Cheng and others blocked the passes and Hong could not get through.

sentences.zh: 議郎董昭以楊奉兵馬最強而少黨援，作操書與奉曰：「吾與次軍聞名慕義，便推赤心。

translations.literal: Consultant Grandee Dong Zhao, because Yang Feng's horses and troops were strongest yet he had few partisan supporters, drafted a letter from Cao to Feng saying: "I and the Second Army, having heard your name, admired your righteousness, and at once offered our loyal hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Consultant Dong Zhao noted that Yang Feng had the strongest force but few allies; he drafted a letter for Cao Cao to Yang Feng: "Your army and mine have long admired each other's reputation and pledged mutual loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今將軍拔萬乘之艱難，反之舊都，翼佐之功，超世無疇，何其休哉！

translations.literal: Now the General has drawn the Son of Heaven out of ten-thousand-carriage difficulties and returned him to his old capital; the achievement of aiding and assisting surpasses the age without peer—how glorious!
translations.idiomatic: You have rescued the emperor from dire peril and restored him to the old capital—an achievement without parallel in our age. How splendid!

sentences.zh: 方今群凶猾夏，四海未寧，神器至重，事在維輔；

translations.literal: At present the many villains are cunning in Xia, the four seas are not yet at peace, the sacred vessel is of utmost weight, and the matter lies in sustaining and assisting;
translations.idiomatic: Traitors still run riot, the realm is not at peace, and the imperial charge is too weighty for any one man;

sentences.zh: 必須眾賢以清王軌，誠非一人所能獨建，心腹四支，實相恃賴，一物不備，則有闕焉。

translations.literal: it must rely on the multitude of worthies to clear the royal path; truly it is not what one man alone can establish—the heart and belly, the four limbs, in fact depend on one another; if one thing is not complete, there is a gap.
translations.idiomatic: it requires many worthy men to restore the royal order. No one can build this alone: heart and limbs must rely on one another, and if any part is missing the whole is flawed.

sentences.zh: 將軍當為內主，吾為外援。

translations.literal: The General should be the inner master; I will be the outer support.
translations.idiomatic: You should be the pillar within; I will be your support from without.

sentences.zh: 今吾有糧，將軍有兵，有無相通，足以相濟，死生契闊，相與共之。

translations.literal: Now I have grain and the General has troops; what one has and the other lacks can be exchanged, sufficient to aid each other—in life and death, in parting and reunion, let us share together.
translations.idiomatic: I have grain and you have troops; together we can supply each other's wants, through life and death, in plenty and in want.

sentences.zh: 」奉得書喜悅，語諸將軍曰：「兗州諸軍近在許耳，有兵有糧，國家所當依仰也。

translations.literal: " Feng received the letter with joy and said to the generals: "The armies of Yan Province are close at Xu; with troops and grain they are what the state should rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng was delighted by the letter and told his officers, "Cao Cao's forces are close at Xu, with both troops and grain—the state ought to rely on them.

sentences.zh: 」遂共表操為鎮東將軍，襲父爵費亭侯。

translations.literal: " They thereupon jointly memorialized to appoint Cao as General Who Pacifies the East, inheriting his father's enfeoffment as Marquis of Feiting.
translations.idiomatic: They jointly petitioned to appoint Cao Cao General Who Pacifies the East and confirm his inheritance of his father's title, Marquis of Feiting.

sentences.zh: 韓暹矜功專恣，董承患之，因潛召操；

translations.literal: Han Xian, relying on his achievements, was arrogant and willful; Dong Cheng was troubled by this and secretly summoned Cao;
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian grew arrogant on his past service; Dong Cheng, alarmed, secretly summoned Cao Cao;

sentences.zh: 操乃將兵詣雒陽。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon led troops to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: who marched his army to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 既至，奏韓暹、張楊之罪。

translations.literal: When he arrived he memorialized the crimes of Han Xian and Zhang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he memorialized against Han Xian and Zhang Yang.

sentences.zh: 暹懼誅，單騎奔楊奉。

translations.literal: Xian feared execution and fled alone on horseback to Yang Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian, fearing execution, fled alone to Yang Feng.

sentences.zh: 帝以暹、楊有翼車駕之功，詔一切勿問。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Xian and Yang had the achievement of aiding the imperial carriage, decreed that all matters be left uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering their service in escorting the imperial carriage, ordered that all charges be dropped.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以曹操領司隸校尉、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Cao Cao was appointed acting Colonel-Director of the Retainers and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day, Cao Cao was made acting Colonel-Director of the Retainers and put in charge of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 操於是誅尚書馮碩等三人，討有罪也；

translations.literal: Cao thereupon executed the Master of Writing Feng Shuo and three others—to punish guilt;
translations.idiomatic: He executed Master of Writing Feng Shuo and two others, punishing the guilty;

sentences.zh: 封衛將軍董承等十三人為列侯，賞有功也；

translations.literal: enfeoffed Palace Guard General Dong Cheng and thirteen others as ranked marquises—to reward achievement;
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffed Palace Guard General Dong Cheng and twelve others as marquises, rewarding merit;

sentences.zh: 贈射聲校尉沮儁為弘農太守，矜死節也。

translations.literal: posthumously appointed Colonel of the Archers Ju Jun as Administrator of Hongnong—to honor death in integrity.
translations.idiomatic: and posthumously appointed Colonel of the Archers Ju Jun Administrator of Hongnong, honoring his martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 操引董昭並坐，問曰：「今孤為此，當施何計？

translations.literal: Cao had Dong Zhao sit with him and asked: "Now that I have done this, what plan should I employ?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao invited Dong Zhao to sit with him and asked, "Now that I have come this far, what course should I take?

sentences.zh: 」昭曰：「將軍興義兵以誅暴亂，入朝天子，輔翼三室，此五伯之功也。

translations.literal: " Zhao said: "The General raised the righteous army to punish violence and disorder, entered court to serve the Son of Heaven, and aided the royal house—this is the achievement of the Five Hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao replied, "You raised the righteous army to suppress rebellion, attended the emperor at court, and supported the royal house—the achievement of a hegemon.

sentences.zh: 此下諸將，人殊意異，未必服從，今留匡弼，事勢不便，惟有移駕幸許耳。

translations.literal: The generals below each have different intentions and may not necessarily obey; to remain now as a supporting minister is inconvenient to the situation—there is only moving the imperial carriage to favor Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The generals here each have his own mind and may not obey you; staying to support the court is awkward. You should move the emperor to Xu.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷播越，新還舊京，遠近跂望，冀一朝獲安，今復徙駕，不厭眾心。

translations.literal: Yet the court has been cast adrift, newly returned to the old capital; near and far stand on tiptoe in hope, expecting peace in a morning—now to move the carriage again will not satisfy the multitude's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court has been uprooted and has only just returned to the old capital; the realm stands on tiptoe hoping for peace. To move the emperor again will disappoint everyone.

sentences.zh: 夫行非常之事，乃有非常之功，願將軍算其多者。

translations.literal: To perform an extraordinary act is to achieve an extraordinary merit; I wish the General would calculate which side has the greater advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Extraordinary deeds yield extraordinary rewards—weigh which course offers the greater gain.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「此孤本志也。

translations.literal: " Cao said: "This has always been my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "That has always been my intent.

sentences.zh: 楊奉近在梁耳，聞其兵精，得無為孤累乎？

translations.literal: Yang Feng is close at Liang; I hear his troops are elite—might he not become a burden to me?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng is nearby at Liang, and I hear his troops are first-rate—will he not become a burden?

sentences.zh: 」昭曰：「奉少黨援，心相憑結，鎮東、費亭之事，皆奉所定，宜進遣使厚遺答謝，以安其意，說『京都無糧，欲車駕暫幸魯陽，魯陽近許，轉運稍易，可無縣乏之憂。

translations.literal: " Zhao said: "Feng has few partisan supporters and his heart is bound to ours; the matters of Pacifying the East and Feiting were all settled by Feng—you should promptly send envoys with generous gifts in reply and thanks to settle his mind, saying: 'The capital has no grain; we wish the imperial carriage temporarily to favor Luyang. Luyang is near Xu; transport will be somewhat easier, and there need be no worry of shortage and exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao said, "Yang Feng has few allies and is already tied to you—the appointments of Pacifying the East and Feiting were his doing. Send envoys with rich gifts to reassure him. Tell him the capital lacks grain and the emperor will temporarily visit Luyang, which is near Xu and easier to supply, so the court need not go hungry.

sentences.zh: 』奉為人勇而寡慮，必不見疑，比使往來，足以定計，奉何能為累！

translations.literal: ' Feng is brave but short on deliberation; he will surely not suspect. By the time envoys go back and forth, plans will be settled—how could Feng become a burden!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng is brave but not deep; he will not suspect you. By the time messengers have gone back and forth, your plan will be set—how can he hinder you?

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Cao said: "Good!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」即遣使詣奉。

translations.literal: " He immediately sent envoys to Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He at once sent envoys to Yang Feng.

translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day, the imperial procession left Huanyuan Pass and headed east. (The Records of Emperor Wu in the Wei Annals dates this event to the ninth month.)

translations.idiomatic: The capital was then moved to Xu.

translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was made Grand General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping.

translations.literal: The ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain were first established at Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain were first established at Xu.

translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Chunyu Jia, Grand Commandant Yang Biao, and Minister of Works Zhang Xi were all removed from office.

sentences.zh: 11車駕之東遷也，楊奉自梁欲邀之，不及。

translations.literal: 11 When the imperial carriage moved east, Yang Feng from Liang wished to intercept it but did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved east, Yang Feng from Liang tried to intercept the procession but arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，曹操征奉，奉南奔袁術，遂攻其梁屯，拔之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Cao Cao campaigned against Feng; Feng fled south to Yuan Shu; Cao then attacked his encampment at Liang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Cao Cao attacked Yang Feng, who fled south to Yuan Shu; Cao then stormed his camp at Liang and captured it.

sentences.zh: 12詔書下袁紹，責以「地廣兵多，而專自樹黨，不聞勤王之師，但擅相討伐。

translations.literal: 12 An imperial edict was sent down to Yuan Shuo, reproaching him: "Your territory is broad and your troops numerous, yet you exclusively build factions of your own; we hear no army coming to aid the king, but only unauthorized mutual attacks.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict rebuked Yuan Shao: "Your lands are vast and your armies numerous, yet you build factions for yourself alone. We hear no troops coming to rescue the throne—only private wars among yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」紹上書深自陳訴，〔十一月〕<ref>〔十一月〕句袁紹為太尉事，《魏志．武帝紀》、《後漢紀》均繫於十月，是月癸巳朔，無戊辰、丙戌。

translations.literal: " Shuo submitted a memorial deeply pleading his own case. [Eleventh month]. [ref: The passage on Yuan Shuo's appointment as Grand Commandant—in the Wei Annals, Records of Emperor Wu, and the Later Han Annals it is placed in the tenth month; that month begins on guisi, and there are no days wuchen or bingxu.]
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao submitted a long defense. In the eleventh month. (Yuan Shao's appointment as Grand Commandant appears in the tenth month in the Wei Annals and Later Han Annals; that month began on guisi, so wuchen and bingxu cannot fall within it.)

sentences.zh: 《後漢書．獻帝紀》則繫於十一月，是月壬戌朔，有戊辰、丙戌，《後漢書》是，據補。

translations.idiomatic: The Book of Later Han, Annals of Emperor Xian, places it in the eleventh month, which began on renxu and includes wuchen and bingxu—the Book of Later Han is correct, and the eleventh month is supplied accordingly.

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Shuo was appointed Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Ye; Shuo was shamed to rank below Cao Cao and angrily said: "Cao Cao ought to have died several times over—I repeatedly saved and preserved him—and now he holds the Son of Heaven hostage to command me!
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day, Yuan Shao was made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Ye. Ashamed to rank below Cao Cao, he raged: "Cao Cao should have died a dozen deaths—I kept saving him—and now he holds the emperor hostage to order me about!

sentences.zh: 」表辭不受。

translations.literal: " He memorialized declining and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to decline and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 操懼，請以大將軍讓紹。

translations.literal: Cao was afraid and requested to yield the Grand Generalship to Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, alarmed, offered to yield the Grand Generalship to Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以操為司空，行車騎將軍事。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Cao was appointed Minister of Works and acted in the affairs of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day, Cao Cao was made Minister of Works with concurrent duties as General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 操以荀彧為侍中，守尚書令。

translations.literal: Cao appointed Xun Yu as Palace Attendant and acting Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao appointed Xun Yu Palace Attendant and acting Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 操問彧以策謀之士，彧薦其從子蜀郡太守攸及潁川郭嘉。

translations.literal: Cao asked Yu for men of strategy and planning; Yu recommended his cousin's son the Administrator of Shu Commandery You and Guo Jia of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked Xun Yu for strategists; Xun Yu recommended his cousin Xun You, Administrator of Shu Commandery, and Guo Jia of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 操徵攸為尚書，與語，大悅，曰：「公達，非常人也。

translations.literal: Cao summoned You as Master of Writing; speaking with him, he was greatly pleased and said: "Gongda—you are no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao summoned Xun You as Master of Writing and, after talking with him, exclaimed, "Gongda, you are no ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 吾得與之計事，天下當何憂哉！

translations.literal: If I can plan affairs with him, what should all under Heaven worry about!
translations.idiomatic: With him to plan by my side, what have I to fear under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」以為軍師。

translations.literal: " He was made Military Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military adviser.

sentences.zh: 初，郭嘉往見袁紹，紹甚敬禮之，居數十日，謂紹謀臣辛評、郭圖曰：「夫智者審於量主，故百全而功名可立。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Guo Jia went to see Yuan Shuo; Shuo treated him with great respect and courtesy. After several tens of days he said to Shuo's strategists Xin Ping and Guo Tu: "The wise man weighs his lord carefully; thus he is secure in every way and fame and achievement can be established.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Guo Jia had visited Yuan Shao, who received him with great honor. After some days he told Yuan Shao's advisers Xin Ping and Guo Tu, "A wise man chooses his lord carefully and so preserves himself whole while winning fame.

sentences.zh: 袁公徒欲效周公之下士，而不知用人之機，多端寡要，好謀無決，欲與共濟天下大難，定霸王之業，難矣。

translations.literal: Lord Yuan merely wishes to imitate the Duke of Zhou in humbling himself before scholars, yet does not understand the keys to employing men—many schemes but few essentials, fond of planning but without decision. To wish to cross together the great calamity of all under Heaven and settle the hegemon's and king's enterprise—this is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yuan only imitates the Duke of Zhou in courting scholars, yet does not grasp how to use men—many schemes, few essentials, fond of counsel but unable to decide. To join him in saving the realm and founding an empire would be hard.

sentences.zh: 吾將更舉以求主，子盍去乎！

translations.literal: I shall seek another lord; why do you not leave as well!
translations.idiomatic: I shall look elsewhere for a lord—why do you not leave too?

sentences.zh: 」二人曰：「袁氏有恩德於天下，人多歸之，且今最強，去將何之！

translations.literal: " The two said: "The Yuan clan has grace and virtue toward all under Heaven; many men rally to them, and moreover they are now strongest—if we leave, where shall we go!
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "The Yuan clan has won grace across the realm; men flock to them, and they are now the strongest power—where would we go?

sentences.zh: 」嘉知其不寤，不復言，遂去之。

translations.literal: " Jia knew they would not awaken; he spoke no more and thereupon left.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia saw they would not listen, said no more, and left.

sentences.zh: 操召見，與論天下事，豆曰：「使孤成大業者，必此人也！

translations.literal: Cao summoned him for an audience and discussed affairs of all under Heaven with him; Cao said: "The one who will enable me to complete the great enterprise—surely it is this man!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao received him and discussed the realm with him, then said, "The man who will help me complete the great enterprise is surely this one!

sentences.zh: 」嘉出，亦喜曰：「真吾主也！

translations.literal: " When Jia came out he also said with joy: "Truly this is my lord!
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Jia left he rejoiced, "This is truly my lord!

sentences.zh: 」操表嘉為司空〔軍師〕祭酒<ref>司空〔軍師〕祭酒按《三國志》避司馬師諱省「軍師」二字，今據補。

translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao memorialized to appoint Guo Jia Libationer to the Minister of Works and military adviser. (The Records of the Three Kingdoms omits "military adviser" to avoid the taboo on Sima Shi; the term is supplied here.)

操以山陽滿寵為許令，操從弟洪，有賓客在許界數犯法，寵收治之，洪書報寵，寵不聽。

translations.literal: Cao appointed Man Chong of Shanyang as Magistrate of Xu; Cao's cousin Hong had guests within Xu's borders who repeatedly violated the law; Chong arrested and tried them; Hong wrote to inform Chong, but Chong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao appointed Man Chong of Shanyang magistrate of Xu. Cao Hong, a cousin of Cao Cao, had guests who repeatedly broke the law within Xu's jurisdiction; Man Chong arrested them. Cao Hong wrote to intercede, but Man Chong paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 洪以白操，操尋許主旨，寵知將欲原客，乃速殺之。

translations.literal: Hong reported to Cao; Cao was about to issue an order pardoning the guests on Xu's authority; Chong knew they would soon be pardoned and thereupon quickly executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong appealed to Cao Cao, who was about to issue a pardon; Man Chong, guessing his intent, had the offenders executed at once.

sentences.zh: 操喜曰：「當事不當爾邪！

translations.literal: Cao was pleased and said: "When handling affairs, should one not act thus!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was pleased and said, "Is this not how affairs ought to be handled!

sentences.zh: 13北海太守孔融，負其高氣，志在靖難，而才疏意廣，訖無成功。

translations.literal: 13 Kong Rong, Administrator of Beihai, relied on his lofty spirit; his will was set on quelling calamity, yet his talent was thin and his aims broad—in the end he achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong, Administrator of Beihai, prided himself on his lofty spirit and aspired to save the realm, but his talent was slight and his ambitions vast—in the end he accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 但能張磔網羅，而目理甚疏。

translations.literal: He could only spread nets wide, yet his eye for principle was very loose.
translations.idiomatic: He could cast a wide net, but his grasp of essentials was loose.

sentences.zh: 造次能得人心，久久亦不願附也。

translations.literal: In haste he could win men's hearts, yet over time they were still unwilling to attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: He could win men quickly, but in time they would not stay with him.

sentences.zh: 其所任用，好奇取異，多剽輕小才，至於奠事名儒鄭玄，執子孫禮，易其鄉名曰鄭公鄉，及清儁之士左承祖、劉義遜等，皆備在座席而已，不與論政事，曰：「此民望，不可失也！

translations.literal: Those he employed were fond of the strange and took the unusual; many were flashy light talents. As for the renowned Confucian Zheng Xuan, he performed the rites of host and guest, changed the name of his village to Village of Lord Zheng, and for pure outstanding men such as Zuo Chengzu and Liu Yisun—he merely had them all present at his seat and did not discuss state affairs with them, saying: "These are the people's hopes; they cannot be lost!
translations.idiomatic: Those he employed were drawn to the odd and flashy—mostly shallow talents. For the great scholar Zheng Xuan he performed guest rites as to an elder, renamed his village the Village of Lord Zheng, and for worthy men such as Zuo Chengzu and Liu Yisun he merely kept them at his table without consulting them on policy, saying, "These are men the people esteem—we cannot neglect them!

sentences.zh: 黃巾來寇，融戰敗，走保都昌。

translations.literal: The Yellow Turbans came to raid; Rong was defeated in battle and fled to hold Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yellow Turbans attacked, Kong Rong was defeated and fled to Duchang.

sentences.zh: 時袁、公孫首尾相連，融兵弱糧寡，孤立一隅，不與相通。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan and Gongsun were linked head to tail; Rong's troops were few and grain scant; isolated in a corner, he had no communication with others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan held the north in a chain; Kong Rong's forces were few and his grain scant; isolated in a corner, he had no line of communication.

sentences.zh: 左承祖勸融宜自托強國，融不聽而殺之，劉義遜棄去。

translations.literal: Zuo Chengzu urged Rong that he should attach himself to a strong state; Rong did not listen and killed him; Liu Yisun abandoned him and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Chengzu urged him to submit to a strong power; Kong Rong refused and had him killed. Liu Yisun left him.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史袁譚攻融，自春至夏，戰士所餘纔數百人，流矢交集，而融猶隱-{几}-讀書，談笑自若。

translations.literal: Yuan Tan, Inspector of Qing Province, attacked Rong; from spring to summer the warriors remaining were only several hundred; flying arrows crossed in profusion, yet Rong still leaned on his armrest reading books, talking and laughing as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan, Inspector of Qing Province, besieged him from spring through summer until only a few hundred soldiers remained; arrows flew thick as rain, yet Kong Rong still read at his desk, talking and laughing as though at ease.

sentences.zh: 城夜陷，及奔東山，妻子為譚所虜。

translations.literal: The city fell by night; he fled to the eastern hills; his wife and children were captured by Tan.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell by night; he fled to the eastern hills; Yuan Tan captured his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 曹操與融有舊，徵為將作大匠。

translations.literal: Cao Cao had old ties with Rong and summoned him as Master of Works in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, who knew him of old, summoned him as Master of Works in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 袁譚初至青州，其土自河而西，不過平原。

translations.literal: When Yuan Tan first arrived in Qing Province, its territory west of the river extended no farther than Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Tan first took Qing Province, his lands west of the Yellow River extended only to Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 譚北排田楷，東破孔融，威惠甚著；

translations.literal: Tan drove off Tian Kai to the north and broke Kong Rong to the east; his authority and grace were very manifest;
translations.idiomatic: He drove Tian Kai north, crushed Kong Rong in the east, and won great renown;

sentences.zh: 其後信任群小，肆志奢淫，聲望遂衰。

translations.literal: afterward he trusted petty men, indulged his will in luxury and licentiousness, and his reputation and prestige declined.
translations.idiomatic: but later he trusted petty men, indulged in luxury, and his prestige faded.

sentences.zh: 14中平以來，天下亂離，民棄農業，諸軍並起，率乏糧穀，無終歲之計，飢則寇略，飽則棄餘，瓦解流離，無敵自破者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: 14 Since the Zhongping era, all under Heaven has been in disorder and separation; the people have abandoned agriculture; armies have risen together, generally lacking grain, with no plan for a full year—when hungry they raided and plundered, when full they cast away the surplus; disintegrating and scattering in flight, those who broke apart without an enemy being too many to count.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhongping era the realm had fallen into chaos; peasants abandoned farming; armies rose everywhere, usually short of grain, with no stores for a full year. Hungry, they plundered; sated, they wasted what remained. Countless hosts collapsed without an enemy to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 袁紹在河北，軍人仰食桑椹。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao in Hebei—his soldiers relied on mulberries for food.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's men in Hebei lived on mulberries.

sentences.zh: 袁術在江淮，取給蒲蠃，民多相食，州里蕭條。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu in the Jiang-Huai region took his supply from river mussels and snails; the people often ate one another; the provinces and districts were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu's armies in the Huai region fed on shellfish; cannibalism was common; the provinces lay waste.

sentences.zh: 羽林監棗祗請建置屯田，曹操從之，以祗為屯田都尉，以騎都尉任峻為典農中郎將。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Zao Zhi requested establishing tuntian colonies; Cao Cao followed this and appointed Zhi Colonel-Director of Tuntian and the Commandant of Cavalry Ren Jun Central Gentleman for Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Zao Zhi of the Imperial Guard proposed establishing military colonies; Cao Cao agreed, appointing Zao Zhi Colonel-Director of Tuntian and Ren Jun, Commandant of Cavalry, Central Gentleman for Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 募民屯田許下，得穀百萬斛。

translations.literal: He recruited civilians to farm colonies below Xu and obtained a million hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians were settled in colonies near Xu and produced a million hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 於是州郡倒置田官，所在積穀，倉廩皆滿。

translations.literal: Thereupon provinces and commanderies everywhere established agricultural officials; grain accumulated wherever they were, and granaries were all full.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies followed suit; grain piled up everywhere and granaries filled.

sentences.zh: 故操征伐四方，無運糧之勞，遂能兼併群雄。

translations.literal: Thus when Cao campaigned in the four directions he had no labor of transporting grain and was able to annex the many heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Cao Cao campaigned in every direction without the burden of long supply lines and was able to swallow rival warlords one by one.

sentences.zh: 軍國之饒，起於祗而成於峻。

translations.literal: The abundance of army and state began with Zhi and was completed by Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The wealth of his armies and state began with Zao Zhi and was brought to fruition by Ren Jun.

sentences.zh: 15袁術畏呂布為己害，乃為子求婚，布復許之，術遣將紀靈等步騎三萬攻劉備，備求救於布。

translations.literal: 15 Yuan Shu feared Lü Bu would harm him and therefore arranged a marriage for his son; Bu again promised it. Shu sent his general Ji Ling and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Liu Bei; Bei sought rescue from Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, fearing Lü Bu, betrothed his son to Lü Bu's family; Lü Bu agreed again. Yuan Shu sent Ji Ling with thirty thousand foot and horse to attack Liu Bei, who appealed to Lü Bu for help.

sentences.zh: 諸將謂布曰：「將軍常欲殺劉備，今可假手於術。

translations.literal: The generals said to Bu: "The General has often wished to kill Liu Bei—now you can borrow Shu's hand.
translations.idiomatic: His officers said, "You have often wanted Liu Bei dead—let Yuan Shu do it for you.

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Bu said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu said, "No.

sentences.zh: 術若破備，則北連泰山諸將，吾為在術圍中，不得不救也。

translations.literal: If Shu breaks Bei, he will link north with the generals of Mount Tai; I will be within Shu's encirclement and cannot but rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuan Shu defeats Liu Bei, he will join the Taishan commanders to the north and surround me—I must save Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 」便率步騎千餘馳往赴之。

translations.literal: " He immediately led more than a thousand infantry and cavalry galloping to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: He led more than a thousand foot and horse to Liu Bei's relief.

sentences.zh: 靈等聞布至，皆斂兵而止。

translations.literal: When Ling and the others heard Bu had arrived, they all drew in their troops and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Ling heard Lü Bu was coming, he halted his army.

sentences.zh: 布屯沛城西南，遣鈴下請靈等，靈等亦請布，布往就之，與備共飲食。

translations.literal: Bu encamped southwest of Pei city, sent orderlies to invite Ling and the others; Ling and the others also invited Bu; Bu went to join them and feasted together with Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu camped southwest of Pei and sent orderlies to summon Ji Ling; Ji Ling in turn invited Lü Bu, who came and dined with Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 布謂靈等曰：「玄德，布弟也，為諸君所困，故來救之。

translations.literal: Bu said to Ling and the others: "Xuande is Bu's younger brother; he was trapped by you gentlemen, so I came to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu told Ji Ling and his officers, "Xuande is my sworn brother. You had him cornered, so I came to save him.

sentences.zh: 布性不喜合鬥，喜解鬥耳。

translations.literal: Bu's nature dislikes joining in battle; he likes only resolving battles.
translations.idiomatic: I do not love fighting—I love ending fights.

sentences.zh: 」乃令軍候植戟於營門，布彎弓顧曰：「諸君觀布射戟小支，中者當各解兵，不中可留決鬥。

translations.literal: He then ordered army attendants to plant halberds at the camp gate; Bu bent his bow, looked back, and said: "Gentlemen, watch Bu shoot the halberd's small branch—if I hit it, each of you shall disband your troops; if I miss, you may stay and fight it out."
translations.idiomatic: He had halberds set up at the camp gate, drew his bow, and called out, "Watch me strike the side branch of that halberd. If I hit it, disband your armies. If I miss, stay and fight."

sentences.zh: 」布即一發，正中戟支。

translations.literal: With one shot Bu immediately hit the halberd branch squarely.
translations.idiomatic: With a single arrow he struck the branch dead center.

sentences.zh: 靈等皆驚，言：「將軍天威也！

translations.literal: Ling and the others were all startled and said: "General, this is heaven's might!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ling and his men were astonished. "General," they cried, "this is the power of Heaven itself!"

sentences.zh: 」明日復歡會，然後各罷。

translations.literal: The next day they met again in merriment, and then each withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They feasted again the next day, then each army went its way.

sentences.zh: 備合兵得萬餘人，布惡之，自出兵攻備。

translations.literal: Bei combined his forces and obtained more than ten thousand men; Bu hated this and himself led troops to attack Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei gathered more than ten thousand troops. Lü Bu, alarmed, marched out and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 備敗走，歸曹操，操厚遇之，以為豫州牧。

translations.literal: Bei was defeated and fled, returning to Cao Cao; Cao treated him generously and made him Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was beaten and fled to Cao Cao, who received him warmly and appointed him Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 或謂操曰：「備有英雄之志，今不早圖，後必為患。

translations.literal: Someone advised Cao, saying: "Bei has the will of a hero; if you do not plot against him early, he will surely be a trouble later."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Cao Cao, "Liu Bei has the heart of a hero. If you do not deal with him now, he will become a menace later."

sentences.zh: 」操以問郭嘉，嘉曰：「有是。

translations.literal: Cao asked Guo Jia about it; Jia said: "That is so.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao consulted Guo Jia. Guo Jia said, "That is true.

sentences.zh: 然公起義兵，為百姓除暴，推誠杖信以招俊傑，猶懼其未也。

translations.literal: Yet the lord raised a righteous army to remove violence for the common people, pushing sincerity and leaning on trust to recruit outstanding men—you still fear it is not enough.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you raised a righteous army to deliver the people from tyranny, winning men of talent with sincerity and trust—and you still worry it is not enough.

sentences.zh: 今備有英雄名，以窮歸己而害之，是以害賢為名也。

translations.literal: Now Bei has a hero's fame; because he is exhausted he has come to you, yet if you harm him, you will bear the name of harming the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei bears the name of a hero. He comes to you in distress; to harm him now would mark you as one who destroys the worthy.

sentences.zh: 如此，則智士將自疑，回心擇主，公誰與定天下乎！

translations.literal: If so, wise gentlemen will themselves grow doubtful, turn their hearts, and choose another lord—with whom will you settle all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Then every able man will doubt you and turn elsewhere for a lord. With whom will you conquer the realm?

sentences.zh: 夫除一人之患以沮四海之望，安危之機也，不可不察。

translations.literal: To remove one man's trouble yet obstruct the hopes of the four seas—this is the hinge of safety and danger; it cannot go unexamined."
translations.idiomatic: To remove one man's threat while dashing the hopes of the empire—that bears on your very survival. You must weigh it carefully."

sentences.zh: 」操笑曰：「君得之矣！

translations.literal: Cao laughed and said: "You have grasped it!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed. "You have it exactly right!"

sentences.zh: 」遂益其兵，給糧食，使東至沛，收散兵以圖呂布。

translations.literal: He thereupon increased Bei's troops, gave him grain, and sent him east to Pei to gather scattered soldiers and plot against Lü Bu.
translations.idiomatic: He enlarged Liu Bei's force, supplied him with grain, and sent him east to Pei to rally scattered troops against Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 初，備在豫州，舉陳郡袁渙為茂才。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Bei was in Yuzhou, he nominated Yuan Huan of Chen commandery as an outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Liu Bei held Yuzhou, he had nominated Yuan Huan of Chen commandery as a distinguished scholar.

sentences.zh: 渙為呂布所留，布欲使渙作書罵辱備，渙不可，再三強之。

translations.literal: Huan was detained by Lü Bu; Bu wished to make Huan compose a letter cursing and insulting Bei, but Huan would not—though Bu strongly urged him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huan was held by Lü Bu, who wanted him to write a letter reviling Liu Bei. Yuan Huan refused, though Lü Bu pressed him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: He would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He would not agree.

sentences.zh: 布大怒，以兵脅渙曰：「為之則生，不為則死！

translations.literal: Bu was greatly angered and threatened Huan with troops, saying: "Do it and live; refuse and die!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu flew into a rage and threatened him at sword-point: "Write and live; refuse and die!"

sentences.zh: 」渙顏色不變，笑而應之曰：「渙聞唯德可以辱人，不聞以罵。

translations.literal: Huan's countenance did not change; smiling, he answered: "Huan has heard that only virtue can shame a man—I have not heard of shaming by curses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huan's face never altered. Smiling, he replied, "I have heard that only virtue can shame a man—not insults.

sentences.zh: 使彼固君子邪，且不恥將軍之言；

translations.literal: If he is truly a gentleman, he will not even be shamed by the General's words;
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Bei is a true gentleman, your words will not shame him;

sentences.zh: 彼誠小人邪，將復將軍之意，則辱在此不在於彼。

translations.literal: if he is truly a petty man, he will again do as the General wishes—then the shame will be here, not on that side.
translations.idiomatic: if he is a petty man, he will do as you wish anyway—and the shame will be yours, not his.

sentences.zh: 且渙他日之事劉將軍，猶今日之事將軍也，如一旦去此，復罵將軍，可乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, Huan's serving General Liu another day is still today's serving the General; suppose one morning I leave here and again curse the General—would that be permissible!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, my service to General Liu today is like my service to you—if I leave you tomorrow, may I revile you in turn? Would that be right?

sentences.zh: 」布慚而止。

translations.literal: Bu, ashamed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu, abashed, desisted.

sentences.zh: 16張濟自關中引兵入荊州界，攻穰城，為流矢所中死。

translations.literal: 16 Zhang Ji led troops from Guanzhong into Jing province territory, attacked Xiang city, and was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji marched from Guanzhong into Jing province, attacked Xiang, and was killed by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 荊州官屬皆賀，劉表曰：「濟以窮來，主人無禮，至於交鋒，此非牧意，牧受吊，不受賀也。

translations.literal: Jing province's officials all congratulated; Liu Biao said: "Ji came in exhaustion; the host was discourteous, and matters reached the crossing of blades—this was not the shepherd's intent. I receive condolences; I do not accept congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: The officials of Jing province congratulated him, but Liu Biao said, "Zhang Ji came in desperation; we failed him as hosts, and blades were crossed—that was not my wish. I accept condolences, not congratulations."

sentences.zh: 」使人納其眾；

translations.literal: He sent men to bring in Ji's masses;
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to receive Zhang Ji's troops;

sentences.zh: 眾聞之喜，皆歸心焉。

translations.literal: the masses, hearing this, rejoiced and all turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: and when the soldiers heard of it they were glad and gave him their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 濟族子建忠將軍繡代領其眾，屯宛。

translations.literal: Ji's clansman, General Who Establishes Loyalty Xiu, succeeded in leading his masses and encamped at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji's kinsman Zhang Xiu, General Who Establishes Loyalty, took command of the army and encamped at Wan.

sentences.zh: 初，帝既出長安，宣威將軍賈詡上還印綬，往依段煨于華陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning, after the Emperor had left Chang'an, Xuanwei General Jia Xu returned his seal and ribbon and went to rely on Duan Wei at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the emperor left Chang'an, Jia Xu, General Who Displays Might, surrendered his commission and joined Duan Wei at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 詡素知名，為煨軍所望，煨禮奉甚備。

translations.literal: Xu had long been famed; Wei's army looked up to him, and Wei received him with full ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu was already renowned, and Duan Wei's troops revered him; Duan Wei honored him with every courtesy.

sentences.zh: 詡潛謀歸張繡，或曰：「煨待君厚矣，君去安之？

translations.literal: Xu secretly plotted to go to Zhang Xiu; someone said: "Wei treats you generously—where will you go in peace?"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu secretly planned to join Zhang Xiu. Someone asked, "Duan Wei treats you so well—where else could you be safe?"

sentences.zh: 」詡曰：「煨性多疑，有忌詡意，禮雖厚，不可恃久，將為所圖。

translations.literal: Xu said: "Wei is suspicious by nature and is wary of Xu; though his courtesy is thick, one cannot rely on it long—he will plot against me.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu said, "Duan Wei is suspicious by nature and already mistrusts me. His courtesy is lavish, but it will not last—he will turn on me.

sentences.zh: 去必喜，又望吾結大援於外，必厚吾妻子；

translations.literal: If I leave he will surely be glad, and will also hope that I tie a great alliance outside—he will certainly treat my wife and children well;
translations.idiomatic: If I leave he will be pleased, hoping I secure a powerful ally abroad, and he will treat my family well;

sentences.zh: 繡無謀主，亦願得詡：則家與身必俱全矣。

translations.literal: Xiu has no planning master and also wishes to obtain Xu: then family and person will certainly both be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu lacks a strategist and wants me—then both my household and my life will be secure."

sentences.zh: 」詡遂往，繡執子孫禮，煨果善視其家。

translations.literal: Xu thereupon went; Xiu received him with a grandson's ritual, and Wei indeed treated his family well.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu went; Zhang Xiu received him as a grandfather would a grandson, and Duan Wei indeed cared for his family.

sentences.zh: 詡說繡附於劉表，繡從之。

translations.literal: Xu urged Xiu to attach to Liu Biao, and Xiu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu urged Zhang Xiu to submit to Liu Biao, and Zhang Xiu agreed.

sentences.zh: 詡往見表，表以客禮待之。

translations.literal: Xu went to see Biao; Biao treated him with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu visited Liu Biao, who received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 詡曰：「表，平世三公才也，不見事變，多疑無決，無能為也！

translations.literal: Xu said: "Biao has the talent of a Three Ducal rank holder in peaceful times; he does not see affairs changing, is suspicious and without decision—he can accomplish nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu said, "Liu Biao has the talent of a grand minister in peacetime, but he cannot read the times, is suspicious and indecisive—he will achieve nothing!"

sentences.zh: 劉表愛民養士，從容自保，境內無事，關西、兗、豫學士歸之者以千數。

translations.literal: Liu Biao loved the people and nurtured scholars, at ease in protecting himself; within his borders there was no trouble, and scholars from Guanzhong, Yan, and Yu who came to him numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao cherished his people and cultivated scholars, content to hold his own territory in peace. Within his borders all was quiet, and scholars from Guanzhong, Yan, and Yu flocked to him by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 表乃起立學校，講明經術，命故雅樂郎河南杜夔作雅樂。

translations.literal: Biao thereupon established schools, expounded the classics, and ordered the former Elegant Music Gentleman Du Kui of Henan to compose elegant music.
translations.idiomatic: He founded schools, lectured on the classics, and commissioned Du Kui of Henan, former Gentleman of Elegant Music, to restore the court ritual music.

sentences.zh: 樂備，表欲庭觀之。

translations.literal: When the music was complete, Biao wished to view it in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was ready, Liu Biao wished to hear it performed in his hall.

sentences.zh: 夔曰：「今將軍號不為天子，合樂而庭作之，無乃不可乎！

translations.literal: Kui said: "Now the General's title is not Son of Heaven; to combine the music and perform it in the courtyard—perhaps this cannot be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Du Kui said, "You are not the Son of Heaven. To assemble full court music and perform it in the open court—surely that is not permitted!"

sentences.zh: 」表乃止。

translations.literal: Biao thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao desisted.

sentences.zh: 平原禰衡，少有才辨，而尚氣剛傲，孔融薦之於曹操。

translations.literal: Mi Heng of Pingyuan, in his youth, had talent in debate, yet cherished his spirit and was boldly arrogant; Kong Rong recommended him to Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng of Pingyuan was gifted and eloquent but proud and overbearing; Kong Rong recommended him to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 衡罵辱操，操怒，謂融曰：「禰衡豎子，孤殺之，猶雀鼠耳；

translations.literal: Heng cursed and insulted Cao; Cao was angered and told Rong: "Mi Heng is a stripling; if I kill him it is still like a sparrow or a rat;
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng reviled Cao Cao to his face. Cao Cao, furious, told Kong Rong, "Mi Heng is a whelp. I could kill him as easily as a sparrow or a mouse;

sentences.zh: 顧此人素有虛名，遠近將謂孤不能容之。

translations.literal: only this man has long had an empty fame; far and near will say I cannot tolerate him."
translations.idiomatic: but he has a hollow reputation, and men far and near will say I cannot bear talent."

sentences.zh: 」乃送與劉表，表延禮以為上賓。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent him to Liu Biao; Biao extended ritual and made him a honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: So he sent Mi Heng to Liu Biao, who honored him as a chief guest.

sentences.zh: 衡稱表之美盈口，而好議貶其左右，於是左右因形而譖之曰：「衡稱將軍之仁，西伯不過也，唯以為不能斷，終不濟者，必由此也。

translations.literal: Heng praised Biao's virtues with a full mouth, yet liked to discuss and denigrate those at his side; so those at his side, using his manner as a pretext, slandered him, saying: "Heng praises the General's benevolence—no more than the Duke of the West—but thinks he cannot decide; in the end he cannot succeed—this must be from that."
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng praised Liu Biao to the skies, yet loved to criticize those around him. His attendants therefore twisted his words and reported, "Mi Heng says your kindness rivals King Wen of Zhou—but that you cannot decide anything and will never succeed."

sentences.zh: 」其言實指表短，而非衡所言也。

translations.literal: Their words really pointed at Biao's shortcomings, not what Heng had spoken.
translations.idiomatic: That was their own jab at Liu Biao's weakness—not Mi Heng's words at all.

sentences.zh: 表由是怒，以江夏太守黃祖性急，送衡與之，祖亦善街焉。

translations.literal: Biao from this was angered; because Jiangxia Administrator Huang Zu was urgent by nature, he sent Heng to him; Zu also treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao, enraged, sent Mi Heng to Huang Zu, Administrator of Jiangxia, who was hot-tempered by nature; Huang Zu nevertheless received him kindly.

sentences.zh: 後衡眾辱祖，祖殺之。

translations.literal: Later Heng publicly insulted Zu, and Zu killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mi Heng humiliated Huang Zu before the whole company, and Huang Zu had him executed.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，曹操討張繡，軍于淯水，繡舉眾降。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, Cao Cao attacked Zhang Xiu and encamped on the Ru River; Xiu raised his masses and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Cao Cao marched against Zhang Xiu and camped on the Ru. Zhang Xiu surrendered with his whole force.

sentences.zh: 操納張濟之妻，繡恨之；

translations.literal: Cao took Zhang Ji's wife; Xiu hated this;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took Zhang Ji's widow; Zhang Xiu resented it;

sentences.zh: 又以金與繡驍將胡車兒，繡聞而疑懼，襲擊操軍，殺操長子昂。

translations.literal: also he gave gold to Xiu's fierce general Hu Che'er; Xiu heard of it and grew suspicious and fearful, raided Cao's army, and killed Cao's eldest son Ang.
translations.idiomatic: and he lavished gold on Zhang Xiu's champion Hu Che'er. Zhang Xiu, alarmed, launched a night attack and killed Cao Cao's eldest son Cao Ang.

sentences.zh: 操中流矢，敗走，校尉典韋與繡力戰，左右死傷略盡，韋被數十創。

translations.literal: Cao was struck by a stray arrow and fled in defeat; Commandant Dian Wei fought strenuously with Xiu; those left and right were dead and wounded nearly to exhaustion; Wei received several tens of wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao himself was wounded by a stray arrow and fled. Commandant Dian Wei fought Zhang Xiu's men until his guards were nearly all dead; he took dozens of wounds.

sentences.zh: 繡兵前搏之，韋雙挾兩人擊殺之，瞋目大罵而死。

translations.literal: Xiu's soldiers advanced to grapple with him; Wei with both arms seized two men, struck and killed them, glared with wide eyes, cursed loudly, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy closed in, Dian Wei seized two men, one in each arm, and crushed them to death, then glared and roared curses until he fell.

sentences.zh: 操收散兵，還住舞陰。

translations.literal: Cao gathered scattered troops and returned to stay at Wuyin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao rallied his broken units and withdrew to Wuyin.

sentences.zh: 繡率騎來追，操擊破之，繡走還穰，復與劉表合。

translations.literal: Xiu led cavalry in pursuit; Cao broke and defeated them; Xiu fled back to Xiang and again joined Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu pursued with cavalry; Cao Cao routed him. Zhang Xiu fled to Xiang and again allied with Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸軍大亂，平虜校尉泰山于禁獨整眾而還，道逢青州兵劫掠人，禁數其罪而擊之。

translations.literal: At this time the armies were in great disorder; Pacifying Barbarians Commandant Yu Jin of Taishan alone put his masses in order and returned; on the road he met Qing province soldiers plundering people and counted their crimes and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: The army was in chaos, but Yu Jin of Taishan, Pacifying Barbarians Commandant, alone kept his men in formation on the retreat. On the road he met Qing province troops robbing civilians, listed their crimes, and attacked them.

sentences.zh: 青州兵走，詣操。

translations.literal: The Qing province soldiers fled and went to report to Cao.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing province soldiers fled to Cao Cao and lodged a complaint.

sentences.zh: 禁既至，先立營壘，不時謁操。

translations.literal: Jin having arrived, first established camp ramparts and did not promptly pay respects to Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin reached headquarters, pitched camp, and did not hurry to see Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 或謂禁：「青州兵已訴君矣，宜促詣公辨之。
