translations.literal: Someone told Jin: "The Qing province soldiers have already accused you—you should hasten to the lord to explain."
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, "The Qing province men have already denounced you—you should go explain yourself at once."

sentences.zh: 」禁曰：「今賊在後，追至無時，不先為備，何以待敵！

translations.literal: Jin said: "Now bandits are behind; pursuit may arrive without a moment's delay—if I do not first make preparations, with what shall I await the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin said, "The enemy is behind us. Pursuit may strike at any moment—if I do not fortify first, how can I face the foe?

sentences.zh: 且公聰明，譖訴何緣得行！

translations.literal: Moreover the lord is intelligent—how could a slanderous accusation obtain passage!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the lord is wise—what slander could stand against me?"

sentences.zh: 」徐鑿塹安營訖，乃入謁，具陳其狀。

translations.literal: Slowly he dug moats, settled the camp, and then entered to pay respects, fully stating the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He dug trenches, finished his camp, and only then went in to report the full story.

sentences.zh: 操悅，謂禁曰：「淯水之難，吾猶狼狽，將軍在亂能整，討暴堅壘，有不可動之節，雖古名將，何以加之！

translations.literal: Cao was pleased and told Jin: "At the Ru River's difficulty I was still in distress; the General in chaos could put troops in order, punish violence, and firmly establish ramparts, with integrity that cannot be moved—even ancient famed generals—how could one add to that!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was delighted and said, "At the disaster on the Ru I was in utter disorder. You kept your ranks, punished marauders, and built a firm camp with unshakable discipline—even the great generals of old could not match you!"

sentences.zh: 於是錄禁前後功，封益壽亭侯。

translations.literal: He thereupon recorded Jin's achievements before and after and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yishou.
translations.idiomatic: He tallied Yu Jin's past and present service and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yishou.

sentences.zh: 操引軍還許。

translations.literal: Cao led his army back to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao led his army back to Xu.

sentences.zh: 2袁紹與操書，辭語驕慢。

translations.literal: 2 Yuan Shao sent Cao a letter with words and phrases arrogant and slow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao wrote to Cao Cao in language proud and contemptuous.

sentences.zh: 操謂荀彧、郭嘉曰：「今將討不義而力不敵，何如？

translations.literal: Cao told Xun Yu and Guo Jia: "Now I wish to attack the unrighteous yet my strength does not match—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked Xun Yu and Guo Jia, "I mean to punish this rebel, but my force is weaker—what should I do?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「劉、項之不敵，公所知也。

translations.literal: They replied: "Liu Bang and Xiang Yu's not being equal—you know it.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "You know how unequal Liu Bang and Xiang Yu were.

sentences.zh: 漢祖唯智勝項羽，故羽雖強，終為所禽。

translations.literal: The Han founder overcame Xiang Yu only by wisdom; so though Yu was strong, in the end he was captured by him.
translations.idiomatic: The founder of Han overcame Xiang Yu by wisdom alone; though Xiang Yu was mighty, in the end Liu Bang took him.

sentences.zh: 今紹有十敗，公有十勝，紹雖強，無能為也。

translations.literal: Now Shao has ten defeats and the lord has ten victories; though Shao is strong, he can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao has ten faults and you have ten strengths. However strong he is, he cannot prevail."

sentences.zh: 紹繁禮多儀，公體任自然，此道勝也；

translations.literal: Shao is profuse in ritual and many in ceremony; the lord's body trusts the natural—this is victory in the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is ceremonious and rigid; you are natural and unforced—a victory of principle;

sentences.zh: 紹以逆動，公奉順以率天下，此義勝也；

translations.literal: Shao moves by rebellion; the lord upholds obedience to lead all under Heaven—this is victory in righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao acts as a rebel; you hold to loyalty and lead the realm—a victory of righteousness;

sentences.zh: 桓、靈以來，政失於寬，紹以寬濟寬，故不攝，公糾之以猛〔而〕上下知制<ref>公糾之以猛〔而〕上下知制據章注及《魏志．郭嘉傳》補。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Huan and Ling, government has failed through excessive leniency; Shao uses leniency to remedy leniency and so cannot restrain; the lord corrects with severity [and] upper and lower know regulation<ref>公糾之以猛〔而〕上下知制 Supplemented according to Zhang's commentary and the Biography of Guo Jia in the Book of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reigns of Huan and Ling, rule has collapsed through indulgence; Yuan Shao meets laxness with laxness and cannot govern; you correct with severity and all ranks know their bounds. (The phrase "corrects with severity and upper and lower know regulation" is supplemented from Zhang's commentary and the Biography of Guo Jia in the Book of Wei.)

sentences.zh: </ref>，此治勝也；

translations.literal: </ref>—this is victory in governance;
translations.idiomatic: ]—a victory in governance;

sentences.zh: 紹外寬內忌，用人而疑之，所任唯親戚子弟，公外易簡而內機明，用人無疑，唯才所宜，不問遠近，此度勝也；

translations.literal: Shao is outwardly lenient and inwardly jealous, employs men yet suspects them, and those he appoints are only kin and younger clansmen; the lord is outwardly easy and simple yet inwardly perceptive, employs men without doubt, and only according to talent—without asking near or far—this is victory in magnanimity;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is generous in show but jealous within, uses men yet distrusts them, and favors only kin; you are open and plain outside yet sharp within, employ men without suspicion, and place each where his talent fits, near or far—a victory of breadth;

sentences.zh: 紹多謀少決，失在後事，公得策輒行，應變無窮，此謀勝也；

translations.literal: Shao has many plans but few decisions and fails by lagging behind events; the lord obtains a stratagem and immediately acts, responding to change without limit—this is victory in planning;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao plots much but decides little and is always behind events; you seize a plan and act at once, adapting without end—a victory of strategy;

sentences.zh: 紹高議揖讓以收名譽，士之好言飾外者多歸之，公以至心待人，不為虛美，士之忠正遠見而有實者皆願為用，此德勝也；

translations.literal: Shao discourses loftily on yielding to gather reputation; many scholars who love fine words and adorn the exterior return to him; the lord treats men with utmost sincerity and does not make empty praise; scholars who are loyal, upright, far-seeing, and substantial all wish to serve you—this is victory in virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao courts fame with lofty courtesy and draws men who love fine speech; you treat men with whole heart and no empty flattery, and the loyal, far-sighted, and solid serve you—a victory of character;

sentences.zh: 紹見人飢寒，恤念之，形於顏色，其所不見，慮或不及，公於目前小事，時有所忽，至於大事，與四海接，恩之所加，皆過其望，雖所不見，慮無不周，此仁勝也；

translations.literal: Shao, seeing men hungry and cold, pities them and shows it on his face; for those he does not see, his thought perhaps does not reach; the lord on small matters before his eyes sometimes neglects, yet on great matters, connecting with the four seas, wherever his grace extends it surpasses their hopes—even what he does not see, his thought has no place it does not reach—this is victory in benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao pities hunger and cold he sees and shows it in his face, yet forgets what he does not see; you may overlook trifles before you, yet on great affairs that touch the empire your kindness exceeds every hope, and even the unseen never escapes your care—a victory of humanity;

sentences.zh: 紹大臣爭權，讒言惑亂，公御下以道，浸潤不行，此明勝也；

translations.literal: Shao's great ministers contend for power and slander confuses; the lord governs subordinates by the Way and seeping slander cannot operate—this is victory in clarity;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's ministers fight for power and slander runs wild; you rule your men by principle and insidious talk cannot take hold—a victory of clarity;

sentences.zh: 紹是非不可知，公所是進之以禮，所不是正之以法，此文勝也；

translations.literal: Shao's right and wrong cannot be known; what the lord approves he advances with ritual, what he disapproves he corrects with law—this is victory in culture;
translations.idiomatic: With Yuan Shao no one knows what is approved or condemned; you advance the worthy with ritual and correct the wrong with law—a victory of civil order;

sentences.zh: 紹好為虛勢，不知兵要，公以少克眾，用兵如神，軍人恃之，敵人畏之，此武勝也。

translations.literal: Shao loves making empty show of force and does not know the essentials of war; the lord with few overcomes the many and uses troops like a spirit—soldiers rely on him and enemies fear him—this is victory in arms."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao loves grand display and does not grasp war; you defeat the many with the few and command like a god—your soldiers trust you and your foes dread you—a victory of arms."

sentences.zh: 」操笑曰：「如卿所言，孤何德以堪之！

translations.literal: Cao laughed and said: "As you gentlemen speak, with what virtue could I bear it!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed. "If all that is true, what virtue have I to deserve it!"

sentences.zh: 」嘉又曰：「紹方北擊公孫瓚，可因其遠征，東取呂布。

translations.literal: Jia also said: "Shao is just then attacking Gongsun Zan in the north; you can take advantage of his distant expedition and seize Lü Bu in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia added, "Yuan Shao is campaigning north against Gongsun Zan. Use his absence to strike Lü Bu in the east.

sentences.zh: 若紹為寇，布為之援，此深害也。

translations.literal: If Shao becomes a raider and Bu is his support, this is a deep harm."
translations.idiomatic: If Yuan Shao raids you and Lü Bu aids him, the danger will be grave."

sentences.zh: 」彧曰：「不先取呂布，河北未易圖也。

translations.literal: Yu said: "If you do not first take Lü Bu, the north of the Yellow River will not be easy to plot."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said, "Unless you destroy Lü Bu first, you cannot hope to take the north."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「然。

translations.literal: Cao said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "True.

sentences.zh: 吾所惑者，又恐紹侵擾關中，西亂羌、胡，南誘蜀、漢，是我獨以兗、豫抗天下六分之五也。

translations.literal: What troubles me is also fearing that Shao will harass Guanzhong, stir the Qiang and Hu in the west, and entice Shu and Han in the south—then I alone with Yan and Yu would resist five-sixths of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I also fear Yuan Shao may trouble Guanzhong, rouse the Qiang and Hu in the west, and win Shu and Han in the south—leaving me with only Yan and Yu to face five parts in six of the realm.

sentences.zh: 為將奈何？

translations.literal: As a general, what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: What is a commander to do?"

sentences.zh: 」彧曰：「關中將帥以十數，莫能相一，唯韓遂、馬騰最強。

translations.literal: Yu said: "The generals of Guanzhong number in the tens and cannot unite as one; only Han Sui and Ma Teng are strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said, "The warlords of Guanzhong are many and divided; only Han Sui and Ma Teng are strongest.

sentences.zh: 彼見山東之爭，必備擁眾自保，今若撫以恩德，遣使連和，雖不能久安，比公安定山東，足以不動。

translations.literal: Seeing the struggle east of the mountains, they will surely arm their masses to protect themselves; if now you soothe them with grace and send envoys to ally with them, though it cannot long endure, compared with your settling the east in security it will be enough that they do not move.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the war in the east, they will hoard their strength. Win them with kindness and treaties; the peace may not last, but it will hold until you secure the east.

sentences.zh: 侍中、尚書僕射鐘繇有智謀，若屬以西事，公無憂矣。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhong Yao has wisdom and planning; if you entrust the western affairs to him, the lord will have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao, Palace Attendant and Vice Director of the Secretariat, is shrewd. Put the west in his hands and you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 」操乃表繇以侍中守司隸校尉，持節督關中諸軍，特使不拘科制。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon memorialized to appoint Yao as Palace Attendant acting as Director of the Retainers, bearing credentials to supervise the armies of Guanzhong, with special envoy authority not bound by standard regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao memorialized to appoint Zhong Yao Palace Attendant and acting Director of the Retainers, with credentials to command the armies of Guanzhong under extraordinary powers.

sentences.zh: 繇至長安，移書騰、遂等，為陳禍福，騰、遂各遣子入侍。

translations.literal: Yao reached Chang'an and sent letters to Teng, Sui, and the others, setting forth fortune and calamity; Teng and Sui each sent their sons to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao reached Chang'an, wrote to Ma Teng and Han Sui explaining the stakes, and each sent his son to the court as hostage.

sentences.zh: 3袁術稱帝於壽春，自稱仲家，以九江太守為淮南尹，置公卿百官，郊祀天地。

translations.literal: 3 Yuan Shu proclaimed himself emperor at Shouchun, styled himself founder of the Second Dynasty, made the Administrator of Jiujiang Chancellor of Huainan, established dukes, ministers, and the full bureaucracy, and performed suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Yuan Shu declared himself emperor at Shouchun, took the title founder of a second imperial house, appointed his Jiujiang administrator Chancellor of Huainan, set up a full court of dukes and ministers, and sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 沛相陳珪，球弟子也，少與術游。

translations.literal: Chen Gui, Chancellor of Pei, was a nephew of Chen Qiu and had been friendly with Yuan Shu in his youth.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui, the chancellor of Pei, was Chen Qiu's nephew and had known Yuan Shu since they were young.

sentences.zh: 術以書召珪，又劫質其子，期必致珪。

translations.literal: Shu summoned Gui by letter and also seized his son as a hostage, expecting that Gui must come.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu summoned Chen Gui by letter and took his son hostage, insisting that Gui must appear.

sentences.zh: 珪答書曰：「曹將軍興復典刑，將撥平凶慝，以為足下當戮力同心。

translations.literal: Gui replied in a letter, saying: "General Cao is restoring the proper punishments and will sweep away the wicked; I believe you ought to unite your strength in the same cause.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui wrote back: "General Cao is restoring lawful government and will uproot the wicked. You ought to join him with all your strength.

sentences.zh: 匡翼漢室。

translations.literal: Support and assist the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: Support the Han dynasty.

sentences.zh: 而陰謀不軌，以身試禍，欲吾營私阿附，有死不能也。

translations.literal: Yet you secretly plot rebellion, bringing disaster on yourself, and wish me to curry favor for private gain—I could not do it though it cost my life.
translations.idiomatic: Instead you plot treason in secret and court your own ruin, yet you want me to flatter you for private gain. I would die before I did that.

sentences.zh: 」術欲以故兗州刺史金尚為太尉，尚不許而逃去，術殺之。

translations.literal: " Yuan Shu wished to appoint the former Inspector of Yanzhou Jin Shang as Grand Commandant; Shang refused and fled; Shu had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu tried to make the former Inspector of Yanzhou, Jin Shang, Grand Commandant. Shang refused and fled; Yuan Shu had him executed.

sentences.zh: 4三月，詔將作大匠孔融持節拜袁紹大將軍，兼督冀、青、幽、并四州。

translations.literal: 4 In the third month, an edict ordered the Master of Works Kong Rong to proceed with credentials and invest Yuan Shao as Grand General, with concurrent supervision of the four provinces Ji, Qing, You, and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: 4 In the third month, the court ordered Master of Works Kong Rong to proceed with imperial credentials and appoint Yuan Shao Grand General with authority over Ji, Qing, You, and Bing.

sentences.zh: 5夏，五月，蝗。

translations.literal: 5 In summer, the fifth month, locusts.
translations.idiomatic: 5 In summer, in the fifth month, locusts ravaged the land.

sentences.zh: 6袁術遣使者韓胤以稱帝事告呂布，因求迎婦，布遣女隨之。

translations.literal: 6 Yuan Shu sent his envoy Han Yin to inform Lü Bu of his assumption of imperial title and also to request a marriage alliance; Bu sent his daughter to go with the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: 6 Yuan Shu sent his envoy Han Yin to tell Lü Bu that he had declared himself emperor and to ask for a marriage alliance. Lü Bu sent his daughter to accompany the envoy.

sentences.zh: 陳珪恐徐、揚合從，為難未已，往說布曰：「曹公奉迎天子，輔贊國政，將軍宜與協同策謀。

translations.literal: Chen Gui, fearing that Xu and Yang might join forces and that troubles would continue without end, went to persuade Bu, saying: "Lord Cao is receiving the Son of Heaven and assisting in state affairs; the General ought to cooperate with him in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui feared that Xu and Yang would unite and that the fighting would never end. He went to Lü Bu and said, "Lord Cao has received the emperor and is guiding the government. You ought to work with him.

sentences.zh: 共存大計。

translations.literal: Pursue the greater design together.
translations.idiomatic: Pursue the larger strategy together.

sentences.zh: 今與袁術結婚，必受不義之名，將有累卵之危矣！

translations.literal: Now if you marry into Yuan Shu's house, you will certainly bear the name of injustice and face a peril like a tower of eggs!
translations.idiomatic: If you marry into Yuan Shu's clan now, you will earn a reputation for disloyalty and face a danger as precarious as a pile of eggs.

sentences.zh: 」布亦怨術初不己受也，女已在塗，乃追還絕婚，械送韓胤，梟首許市。

translations.literal: " Bu also resented that Shu had at first not accepted him; though his daughter was already on the road, he recalled her and broke off the marriage, sent Han Yin in fetters, and displayed his head in the market at Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu also resented that Yuan Shu had once refused to accept him. Though his daughter was already en route, he recalled her, broke off the engagement, sent Han Yin to Xu in chains, and had his head displayed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 陳珪欲使子登詣曹操，布固不肯。

translations.literal: Chen Gui wished to send his son Deng to Cao Cao; Bu firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui wanted to send his son Chen Deng to Cao Cao, but Lü Bu flatly refused.

sentences.zh: 會詔以布為左將軍，操復遺布手書，深加慰納。

translations.literal: At that time an edict appointed Bu Left General; Cao also sent Bu a personal letter with deep expressions of comfort and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then appointed Lü Bu Left General, and Cao Cao sent him a personal letter full of warm reassurance.

sentences.zh: 布大喜，即遣登奉章謝恩，并答操書。

translations.literal: Bu was greatly pleased and immediately sent Deng to present a memorial thanking for the grace and to reply to Cao's letter.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was delighted and at once sent Chen Deng to present a memorial of thanks and to answer Cao Cao's letter.

sentences.zh: 登見操，因陳布勇而無謀，輕於去就，宜早圖之。

translations.literal: When Deng saw Cao, he reported that Bu was brave but without counsel, light in his coming and going, and ought to be dealt with early.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Deng met Cao Cao, he reported that Lü Bu was brave but reckless, fickle in his allegiances, and ought to be dealt with soon.

sentences.zh: 操曰：「布狼子野心，誠難久養，非卿莫究其情偽。

translations.literal: Cao said: "Bu has the heart of a wolf cub—it is truly hard to keep him long; none but you can fathom his true character.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Lü Bu has the heart of a wolf cub—he truly cannot be kept for long. No one but you can read his true intentions.

sentences.zh: 」即增珪秩中二千石，拜登廣陵太守。

translations.literal: " He immediately raised Gui's rank to court gentleman of two thousand bushels and appointed Deng Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately promoted Chen Gui to the rank of two thousand bushels and appointed Chen Deng administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 臨別，操執登手曰：「東方之事，便以相付。

translations.literal: At parting Cao took Deng's hand and said: "Matters in the east—I entrust them to you.
translations.idiomatic: As Chen Deng was leaving, Cao Cao took his hand and said, "Affairs in the east—I leave them in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」令陰合部眾以為內應。

translations.literal: He ordered him secretly to unite local forces as internal allies.
translations.idiomatic: He told him to rally local forces in secret as inside allies.

sentences.zh: 始，布因登求徐州牧不得，登還，布怒，拔戟斫幾曰：「卿父勸吾協同曹操，絕婚公路；

translations.literal: Earlier, Bu had asked Deng to seek the governorship of Xuzhou and did not obtain it; when Deng returned, Bu was angry, drew his halberd and hacked the table, saying: "Your father urged me to cooperate with Cao Cao and break with Gonglu in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lü Bu had sent Chen Deng to request the governorship of Xuzhou and had been refused. When Deng returned, Lü Bu flew into a rage, drew his halberd, and hacked the table, shouting, "Your father told me to side with Cao Cao and break off my marriage with Yuan Shu;

sentences.zh: 今吾所求無獲，而卿父子並顯重，但為卿所賣耳！

translations.literal: now what I sought I did not gain, yet your father and son are both honored—you have sold me out!
translations.idiomatic: now I got nothing I asked for, while you and your father have both risen high—you sold me out!

sentences.zh: 」登不為動容，徐對之曰：「登見曹公言：『養將軍譬如養虎，當飽其肉，不飽則將噬人。

translations.literal: " Deng showed no change of countenance and slowly replied: "When I saw Lord Cao I said: 'To keep the General is like keeping a tiger—you must fill him with meat, and if not filled he will devour men.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng did not flinch and answered calmly, "When I saw Lord Cao I said, 'Keeping you, General, is like keeping a tiger—you must feed it meat, or it will devour people.

sentences.zh: 』公曰：『不如卿言。

translations.literal: ' The Lord said: 'Not as you say.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao said, 'Not so.

sentences.zh: 譬如養鷹，飢即為用，飽則颺去。

translations.literal: It is like keeping a hawk—when hungry it serves you, when full it flies away.'
translations.idiomatic: It is like keeping a hawk—hungry, it obeys you; full, it flies away.'

sentences.zh: 』其言如此。

translations.literal: That is what was said."
translations.idiomatic: That is what he said."

sentences.zh: 」布意乃解。

translations.literal: Bu's resentment then eased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 袁術遣其大將張勳、橋蕤等與韓暹、楊奉連勢，步騎數萬趣下邳，七道攻布。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu sent his generals Zhang Xun, Qiao Rui, and others to join forces with Han Xian and Yang Feng; infantry and cavalry in tens of thousands pressed on Xiapi and attacked Bu by seven routes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu sent his generals Zhang Xun and Qiao Rui, together with Han Xian and Yang Feng, to unite their forces. Tens of thousands of foot and horse converged on Xiapi and attacked Lü Bu along seven routes.

sentences.zh: 布時有兵三千，馬四百匹，懼其不敵，謂陳珪曰：「今致術軍，卿之由也，為之奈何？

translations.literal: Bu then had three thousand troops and four hundred horses, feared he could not resist, and said to Chen Gui: "Now we have brought Shu's army upon us—through you; what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu had only three thousand men and four hundred horses and feared he could not hold out. He said to Chen Gui, "You brought Yuan Shu's army down on us. What do we do now?"

sentences.zh: 」珪曰：「暹、奉與術，猝合之師耳，謀無素定，不能相維，子登策之，比於連雞，勢不俱棲，立可離也。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Xian, Feng, and Shu are a hastily joined host; their plans were never settled together and they cannot sustain each other. Your son Deng judged them like chickens on the same perch—they cannot lodge together and can quickly be separated."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui said, "Han Xian, Yang Feng, and Yuan Shu are a hastily thrown-together force. They have no settled plan and cannot hold together. Your son Chen Deng compared them to chickens roosting on one perch—they cannot stay together and can be split apart at once."

sentences.zh: 」布用珪策，與暹、奉書曰：「二將軍親拔大駕，而布手殺董卓，俱立功名，今奈何與袁術同為賊乎！

translations.literal: Bu adopted Gui's plan and wrote Xian and Feng: "You two generals personally rescued the imperial carriage, while Bu himself slew Dong Zhuo—we all established merit; how now can you join Yuan Shu as bandits together!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu took Chen Gui's advice and wrote to Han Xian and Yang Feng: "You two personally rescued the emperor, and I myself killed Dong Zhuo—we all won glory. How can you now side with Yuan Shu as rebels?"

sentences.zh: 不如相與並力破術，為國除害。

translations.literal: Better join forces to break Shu and remove this harm for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Join me instead and crush Yuan Shu for the good of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」且許悉以術軍資與之。

translations.literal: He also promised to give them all of Shu's military stores.
translations.idiomatic: He also promised to hand over all of Yuan Shu's supplies and equipment.

sentences.zh: 暹、奉大喜，即回計從布。

translations.literal: Xian and Feng were greatly pleased and immediately reversed their plan to follow Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian and Yang Feng were delighted and at once turned about to follow Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 布進軍，去勳營百步，暹、奉兵同時叫呼，並到勳營，勳等散走，佈兵追擊，斬其將十人首，所殺傷墮水死者殆盡。

translations.literal: Bu advanced; a hundred paces from Xun's camp, Xian's and Feng's troops shouted together and reached Xun's camp at once; Xun and the others scattered and fled; Bu's soldiers pursued, beheaded ten of their officers, and those killed, wounded, and drowned were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu marched forward. A hundred paces from Zhang Xun's camp, Han Xian's and Yang Feng's men shouted as one and stormed the camp together. Zhang Xun's force broke and fled. Lü Bu's troops pursued, beheaded ten enemy officers, and killed or drowned nearly the entire enemy host.

sentences.zh: 布因與暹、奉合軍向壽春，水陸並進，到鐘離，所過虜略，還渡淮北，留書辱術。

translations.literal: Bu then joined Xian and Feng and marched on Shouchun by land and water, reached Zhongli, plundered wherever they passed, recrossed north of the Huai, and left a letter insulting Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu then united with Han Xian and Yang Feng and advanced on Shouchun by land and river. They reached Zhongli, plundered along the way, crossed back north of the Huai, and left a letter mocking Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術自將步騎五千揚兵淮上，布騎皆於水北大咍笑之而還。

translations.literal: Shu personally led five thousand foot and horse to display arms on the Huai; Bu's horsemen all hooted and laughed from north of the river and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu personally led five thousand infantry and cavalry to parade his strength on the south bank of the Huai. Lü Bu's horsemen hooted and jeered from the north bank and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 泰山賊帥臧霸襲琅邪相蕭建於莒，破之。

translations.literal: Zang Ba, bandit chief of Mount Tai, attacked Chancellor of Langye Xiao Jian at Ju and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba, the bandit leader of Mount Tai, attacked Xiao Jian, chancellor of Langye, at Ju and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 霸得建資實，許以賂布而未送，布自往求之。

translations.literal: Ba obtained Jian's stores and goods, promised them as tribute to Bu but did not deliver; Bu went in person to demand them.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba seized Xiao Jian's supplies and wealth, promised them to Lü Bu as tribute but never sent them, so Lü Bu went in person to collect them.

sentences.zh: 其督將高順諫曰：「將軍威名宣播，遠近所畏，何求不得，而自行求賂！

translations.literal: His supervising general Gao Shun remonstrated, saying: "The General's awesome name is proclaimed far and near—all fear you; what could you not obtain, that you go in person to beg for tribute!
translations.idiomatic: His commander Gao Shun urged him, "Your renown spreads far and wide—everyone fears you. What could you not obtain without going yourself to demand a bribe?"

sentences.zh: 萬一不克，豈不損邪？

translations.literal: If by chance you do not succeed, will you not suffer loss?"
translations.idiomatic: If you fail, will you not lose face?"

sentences.zh: 」布不從。

translations.literal: Bu did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既至莒，霸等不測往意，固守拒之，無獲而還。

translations.literal: When he reached Ju, Ba and the others could not gauge his intent and held firm in refusal; he obtained nothing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Ju, Zang Ba and his men could not read his intentions and held the city against him. Lü Bu gained nothing and returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 順為人清白有威嚴，少言辭，所將七百餘兵，號令整齊，每戰必克，名「陷陳營」。

translations.literal: Shun was personally upright and stern, sparing of words; the seven hundred-odd men he commanded had orders neat and regular, and every battle was victory—they were named the "Camp That Breaks the Line."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shun was upright and austere, sparing of speech. The seven hundred-odd men under his command obeyed orders with iron discipline and won every battle. They were called the Camp That Breaks the Line.

sentences.zh: 布後疏順，以魏續有內外之親，奪其兵以與續，及當攻戰，則復令順將，順亦終無恨意。

translations.literal: Later Bu grew distant from Shun; because Wei Xu had kin ties inside and out, he took Shun's troops and gave them to Xu; yet when battle came he again had Shun lead, and Shun to the end held no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Bu grew cool toward Gao Shun. Because Wei Xu had family ties within Lü Bu's circle, Lü Bu stripped Gao Shun of his troops and gave them to Wei Xu; yet when battle came he again put Gao Shun in command, and Gao Shun never bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 布性決易，所以無常，順每諫曰：「將軍舉動，不肯詳思，忽有失得，動輒言『誤』，誤豈可數乎！

translations.literal: Bu's nature was rash and facile, hence his inconstancy; Shun often remonstrated, saying: "The General's actions—you will not think them through carefully; suddenly there is loss or gain, and at every turn you say 'a mistake'—can mistakes be numbered so often!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was impulsive and changeable by nature. Gao Shun often warned him, "General, you act without thinking things through. Suddenly something goes wrong, and you say 'my mistake.' How many times can you call it a mistake?"

sentences.zh: 」布知其忠而不能從。

translations.literal: Bu knew his loyalty but could not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu knew Gao Shun was loyal but could not take his advice.

sentences.zh: 7曹操遣議郎王誧以詔書拜孫策為騎都尉，襲爵烏程侯，領會稽太守，使與呂布及吳郡太守陳瑀共討袁術。

translations.literal: 7 Cao Cao sent Advisory Grandee Wang Xu with an edict to invest Sun Ce as Commandant of Cavalry, to succeed to the marquisate of Wucheng, and to hold concurrently the post of Administrator of Kuaiji, ordering him with Lü Bu and Administrator of Wu Chen Yu to attack Yuan Shu jointly.
translations.idiomatic: 7 Cao Cao sent Advisory Grandee Wang Xu with an imperial edict appointing Sun Ce Commandant of Cavalry, heir to the marquisate of Wucheng, and Administrator of Kuaiji, and ordered him to join Lü Bu and Chen Yu, administrator of Wu commandery, in attacking Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 策欲得將軍號以自重，誧便承製假策明漢將軍。

translations.literal: Ce wished to obtain a general's title for added weight; Xu then on his own authority provisionally made Ce Bright-Han General.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce wanted a general's title to lend him weight. Wang Xu therefore used his discretionary authority to appoint him Bright-Han General.

sentences.zh: 策治嚴，行到錢唐，瑀陰圖襲策，潛結祖郎、嚴白虎等，使為內應。

translations.literal: Ce maintained strict discipline; marching to Qiantang, Yu secretly plotted to surprise Ce, secretly contacting Zu Lang, Yan Baihu, and others to serve as inside response.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce kept strict discipline on the march. When he reached Qiantang, Chen Yu secretly plotted a surprise attack and quietly enlisted Zu Lang, Yan Baihu, and others as inside allies.

sentences.zh: 策覺之，遣其將呂範、徐逸攻瑀於海西；

translations.literal: Ce detected it and sent his generals Lü Fan and Xu Yi to attack Yu at Haixi;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce discovered the plot and sent his generals Lü Fan and Xu Yi to attack Chen Yu at Haixi;

sentences.zh: 瑀敗，單騎奔袁紹。

translations.literal: Yu was defeated and fled alone on horseback to Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu was defeated and fled alone on horseback to Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 8初，陳王寵有勇，善弩射。

translations.literal: 8 Earlier, the King of Chen Chen Chong was brave and skilled in crossbow shooting.
translations.idiomatic: 8 Earlier, Chen Chong, King of Chen, was renowned for courage and skill with the crossbow.

sentences.zh: 黃巾賊起，寵治兵自守，國人畏之，不敢離叛。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans arose, Chong trained troops for self-defense; the people of the state feared him and dared not leave or rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans rose, Chen Chong trained troops to defend his territory. The people feared him and did not dare flee or rebel.

sentences.zh: 國相會稽駱俊素有威恩，是時王侯無復租祿，而數見虜奪，或并日而食，轉死溝壑，而陳獨富強，鄰郡人多歸之，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of the state Lu Jun of Kuaiji had long possessed prestige and kindness; at this time the feudal lords no longer received their allotted revenues, and were repeatedly plundered; some ate only every other day and died in ditches and gullies, but Chen alone was rich and strong; people from neighboring commanderies came to him in great numbers—more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The state chancellor, Lu Jun of Kuaiji, had long enjoyed prestige and goodwill. By then the feudal lords no longer received their stipends and were plundered again and again; some ate only every other day and died in ditches, yet Chen alone remained prosperous. People from neighboring commanderies flocked to him until he had more than a hundred thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 及州郡兵起，寵率眾屯陽夏，自稱輔漢大將軍。

translations.literal: When provincial and commandery forces rose, Chong led his masses to encamp at Yangxia and styled himself Grand General Assisting Han.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial armies mobilized, Chen Chong led his followers to camp at Yangxia and styled himself Grand General Assisting Han.

sentences.zh: 袁術求糧於陳，駱俊拒絕之，術忿恚，遣客詐殺俊及寵，陳由是破敗。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu sought grain from Chen; Lu Jun refused; Shu was furious and sent agents under false pretense to kill Jun and Chong; Chen was thereby ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu asked Chen for grain. Lu Jun refused. Yuan Shu was enraged and sent assassins in disguise to kill Lu Jun and Chen Chong, and Chen was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 9秋，九月，司空曹操東征袁術。

translations.literal: 9 In autumn, the ninth month, Minister of Works Cao Cao marched east against Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: 9 In autumn, in the ninth month, Minister of Works Cao Cao marched east against Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術聞操來，棄軍走，留其將橋蕤等於蘄陽以拒操；

translations.literal: Shu heard Cao was coming, abandoned his army and fled, leaving his generals Qiao Rui and others at Qiyang to resist Cao;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu heard that Cao Cao was coming, abandoned his army, and fled, leaving his generals Qiao Rui and others at Qiyang to hold him off;

sentences.zh: 操擊破蕤等，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Cao attacked and broke them and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao defeated and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 術走渡淮，時天旱歲荒，士民凍餒，術由是遂衰。

translations.literal: Shu fled across the Huai; at the time heaven was dry and the year barren, officers and people froze and starved; Shu thereby declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu fled south across the Huai. Drought and famine gripped the land; soldiers and civilians froze and starved, and Yuan Shu's power collapsed.

sentences.zh: 操辟陳國何夔為掾，問以袁術何如，對曰：「天之所助者順，人之所助者信。

translations.literal: Cao recruited He Kai of Chen as an assistant and asked how Yuan Shu was; Kai replied: "What Heaven aids is obedience; what men aid is trust.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao recruited He Kai of Chen state as an aide and asked his view of Yuan Shu. He Kai answered, "Heaven helps those who follow the Way; men help those who keep faith.

sentences.zh: 術無信順之實而望天人之助，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Shu lacks the reality of trust and obedience yet hopes for the aid of Heaven and men—how can he obtain it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu has neither faith nor obedience, yet he expects help from Heaven and men. How can he succeed?"

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「為國失賢則亡，君不為術所用，亡，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: Cao said: "When a state loses the worthy it perishes; you were not employed by Shu—if he perishes, is it not fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "A state that loses worthy men perishes. Yuan Shu would not employ you. If he falls, is that not just?"

sentences.zh: 」操性嚴，掾屬公事往往加杖；

translations.literal: Cao's nature was severe; assistants on official business were often caned;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was stern by nature and often had his staff beaten for official errors;

sentences.zh: 夔常蓄毒藥，誓死無辱，是以終不見及。

translations.literal: Kai always kept poison, vowing death without dishonor, and thereby never suffered it.
translations.idiomatic: He Kai always carried poison and swore he would die rather than be shamed, and so he was never beaten.

sentences.zh: 沛國許褚，勇力絕人，聚少年及宗族數千家，堅壁以御外寇，淮、汝、陳、梁間皆畏憚之，操徇淮、汝，褚以眾歸操，操曰：「此吾樊噲也！

translations.literal: Xu Chu of Pei had strength and courage beyond others; he gathered young men and clansmen in several thousand households, entrenched behind strong walls against outer raiders; between the Huai, Ru, Chen, and Liang all feared him; Cao pacified the Huai and Ru; Chu brought his masses to submit to Cao; Cao said: "This is my Fan Kuai!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chu of Pei state had strength and courage beyond any rival. He gathered young fighters and clansmen into a force of several thousand households and walled his stronghold against outside raiders. Between the Huai, Ru, Chen, and Liang commanderies everyone feared him. When Cao Cao pacified the Huai and Ru, Xu Chu submitted with his followers. Cao Cao said, "This is my Fan Kuai!"

sentences.zh: 即日拜都尉，引入宿衛，諸從褚俠客，皆以為虎士焉。

translations.literal: That very day he invested him as Commandant and brought him into palace guard service; all the roaming warriors who followed Chu were made tiger guards.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he appointed Xu Chu commandant and brought him into the palace guard. All the fighting men who followed Xu Chu were enrolled as tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 10故太尉楊彪與袁術婚姻，曹操惡之，誣云欲圖廢立，奏收下獄，劾以大逆。

translations.literal: 10 The former Grand Commandant Yang Biao had a marriage tie with Yuan Shu; Cao Cao hated this and falsely charged that he plotted to depose and establish, memorialized to arrest and imprison him, and impeached him for great rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: 10 The former Grand Commandant Yang Biao was related by marriage to Yuan Shu. Cao Cao resented this, falsely accused him of plotting to depose the emperor and set up another, had him arrested and thrown into prison, and charged him with high treason.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠孔融聞之，不及朝服，往見操曰：「楊公四世清德，海內所瞻。

translations.literal: Master of Works Kong Rong heard of it, did not wait for court dress, went to see Cao and said: "Lord Yang's four generations of pure virtue—all within the seas look up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Works Kong Rong heard of it, went to see Cao Cao without waiting to dress for court, and said, "Lord Yang's family has been virtuous for four generations. The whole realm looks up to him.

sentences.zh: 《周書》，父子兄弟，罪不相及，況以袁氏歸罪楊公乎！

translations.literal: The Book of Zhou: father, son, and brothers—guilt does not reach one another; how much less can the Yuan clan's guilt be laid on Lord Yang!"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Zhou says that guilt does not extend from father to son or from brother to brother. How much less can the Yuan clan's crime be pinned on Lord Yang!"

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「此國家之意。

translations.literal: Cao said: "This is the state's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "This is the state's decision."

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「假使成王殺召公，周公可得言不知邪？

translations.literal: Rong said: "Suppose King Cheng killed Duke of Shao—could the Duke of Zhou say he did not know?"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong said, "Suppose King Cheng killed the Duke of Shao—could the Duke of Zhou claim he knew nothing?"

sentences.zh: 」操使許令滿寵按彪獄，融與尚書令荀彧皆屬寵曰：「但當受辭，勿加考掠。

translations.literal: Cao had the magistrate of Xu Man Chong investigate Biao's case; Rong and Director of the Secretariat Xun Yu both charged Chong: "Only take his statement—do not add torment under interrogation."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao put Xu district magistrate Man Chong in charge of Yang Biao's case. Kong Rong and Director of the Secretariat Xun Yu both instructed Man Chong, "Take his confession only—do not torture him under interrogation."

sentences.zh: 」寵一無所報，考訊如法。

translations.literal: Chong made no response to any of this and examined by the law as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong ignored them both and interrogated Yang Biao according to the law.

sentences.zh: 數日，求見操，言之曰：「楊彪考訊，無他辭語。

translations.literal: Several days later he sought audience with Cao and said: "Yang Biao under examination had no other words.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Man Chong asked to see Cao Cao and said, "Under interrogation Yang Biao had nothing else to say.

sentences.zh: 此人有名海內，若罪不明白，必大失民望；

translations.literal: This man is famous within the seas; if the crime is not clear, you will greatly lose the people's expectation;
translations.idiomatic: He is famous throughout the realm. If his guilt is not clear, you will lose the people's trust;

sentences.zh: 竊為明公惜之。

translations.literal: I privately grieve for you, my lord."
translations.idiomatic: and I fear for your reputation, my lord."

sentences.zh: 」操即日赦出彪。

translations.literal: Cao that same day pardoned and released Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pardoned and released Yang Biao that same day.

sentences.zh: 初，彧、融聞寵考掠彪，皆怒；

translations.literal: At first when Yu and Rong heard Chong was torturing Biao under examination, both were angry;
translations.idiomatic: At first Xun Yu and Kong Rong were furious when they heard Man Chong was torturing Yang Biao;

sentences.zh: 及因此得出，乃更善寵。

translations.literal: but because Biao was released through this, they became still more favorable to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: but when Yang Biao was freed because of it, they thought even better of Man Chong.

sentences.zh: 彪見漢室衰微，政在曹氏，遂稱腳攣，積十餘年不行，由是得免於禍。

translations.literal: Biao saw the Han house declining and government in the Cao clan; he then claimed crippled legs, and for more than ten years did not go out, and thereby escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao saw the Han dynasty failing and real power passing to the Cao clan. He then claimed crippled legs and for more than ten years did not leave his house, and so escaped further harm.

sentences.zh: 11馬日磾喪至京師，朝廷議欲加禮，孔融曰：「日磾以上公之尊，秉髦節之使，而曲媚奸臣，為所牽率，王室大臣，豈得以見脅為辭！

translations.literal: 11 When Ma Midi's funeral train reached the capital, the court discussed adding honors; Kong Rong said: "Midi with the honor of the highest lord, bearing the envoy's tally and staff, yet stooped to fawn on a treacherous minister and was led by him—the great minister of the royal house: can one take being coerced as an excuse!
translations.idiomatic: 11 When Ma Midi's funeral cortege reached the capital, the court debated whether to grant him additional honors. Kong Rong said, "Ma Midi held the highest rank and went forth bearing the imperial tally and staff, yet he stooped to flatter a traitorous minister and let himself be led along. A great minister of the royal house—can he excuse himself by saying he was coerced?

sentences.zh: 聖上哀矜舊臣，未忍追案，不宜加禮。

translations.literal: The sage emperor pities old servants and has not borne to pursue the case—honors should not be added."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has shown mercy to an old servant and has not pressed the matter. Additional honors are out of the question."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 金尚喪至京師，詔百官弔祭，拜其子瑋為郎中。

translations.literal: When Jin Shang's funeral came to the capital, an edict ordered the hundred officials to mourn and sacrifice; his son Wei was invested as Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Shang's funeral reached the capital, an edict ordered all officials to mourn and offer sacrifice, and appointed his son Jin Wei a Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 12冬，十一月，曹操復攻張繡，拔湖陽，禽劉表將鄧濟；

translations.literal: 12 In winter, the eleventh month, Cao Cao again attacked Zhang Xiu, took Huyang, and captured Liu Biao's general Deng Ji;
translations.idiomatic: 12 In winter, in the eleventh month, Cao Cao attacked Zhang Xiu again, captured Huyang, and took Liu Biao's general Deng Ji prisoner;

sentences.zh: 又攻舞陰，下之。

translations.literal: he also attacked Wuyin and took it.
translations.idiomatic: he also attacked Wuyin and seized it.

sentences.zh: 13韓暹、楊奉在下邳，寇掠徐、揚間，軍飢餓，辭呂布，欲詣荊州；

translations.literal: 13 Han Xian and Yang Feng were at Xiapi, raiding between Xu and Yang; the army was hungry; they took leave of Lü Bu and wished to go to Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: 13 Han Xian and Yang Feng were at Xiapi, raiding between Xu and Yang. Their army was starving. They asked Lü Bu's leave to go to Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 布不聽。

translations.literal: Bu would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu refused.

sentences.zh: 奉知劉備與布有宿憾，私與備相聞，欲共擊布；

translations.literal: Feng knew Liu Bei and Bu had an old grievance and privately communicated with Bei, wishing to strike Bu together;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng knew Liu Bei and Lü Bu had an old grudge and secretly contacted Liu Bei, proposing that they attack Lü Bu together;

sentences.zh: 備陽許之。

translations.literal: Bei outwardly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei agreed openly.

sentences.zh: 奉引軍詣沛，備請奉入城，飲食未半，於座上縛奉，斬之。

translations.literal: Feng led his army to Pei; Bei invited Feng into the city; before half the meal was done, he bound Feng at his seat and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng led his army to Pei. Liu Bei invited him into the city, and before the meal was half finished he had Yang Feng bound in his seat and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 暹失奉，孤特，與十餘騎歸并州，為抒秋令張宣所殺。

translations.literal: Xian lost Feng and stood alone; with a dozen-odd horsemen he returned to Bingzhou and was killed by the magistrate of Shuqiu Zhang Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian lost Yang Feng and was left alone. With a dozen horsemen he fled to Bing province and was killed by Zhang Xuan, magistrate of Shuqiu.

sentences.zh: 胡才、李樂留河東，才為怨家所殺，樂自病死。

translations.literal: Hu Cai and Li Yue remained in Hedong; Cai was killed by a personal enemy; Yue died of illness on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Cai and Li Yue stayed in Hedong. Hu Cai was killed by a personal enemy; Li Yue died of illness.

sentences.zh: 郭汜為其將伍習所殺。

translations.literal: Guo Si was killed by his officer Wu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si was killed by his officer Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 14潁川杜襲、趙儼、繁欽避亂荊州，劉表俱待以賓禮。

translations.literal: 14 Du Xi, Zhao Yan, and Fan Qin of Yingchuan fled the turmoil to Jingzhou; Liu Biao treated them all with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: 14 Du Xi, Zhao Yan, and Fan Qin of Yingchuan fled the chaos to Jingzhou. Liu Biao received them all as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 欽數見奇於表，襲喻之曰：「吾所以與子俱來者，徒欲全身以待時耳，豈謂劉牧當為撥亂之主而規長者委身哉！

translations.literal: Qin was several times regarded as remarkable by Biao; Xi admonished him, saying: "The reason I came with you was only to preserve life and await the times—did I suppose Prefect Liu would be a lord to set the realm right, that we should plan to commit ourselves to an elder as patron!
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qin repeatedly won Liu Biao's special regard. Du Xi warned him, "I came here with you only to save our skins and wait for better days. Did I think Prefect Liu would be the man to restore order, so that we should pledge ourselves to him as to a patron?"

sentences.zh: 子若見能不已，非吾徒也，吾與子絕矣！

translations.literal: If you, sir, do not cease showing off your talents, you are not of our company; I break with you!
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot stop parading your talents, you are no companion of mine—I break with you!

sentences.zh: 」欽慨然曰：「請敬受命！

translations.literal: " Qin said with deep feeling: "I beg to receive your command with respect!
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qin replied firmly, "I shall obey with all respect!"

sentences.zh: 」及曹操迎天子都許，儼謂欽曰：「曹鎮東必能匡濟華夏，吾知歸矣！

translations.literal: " When Cao Cao welcomed the Son of Heaven and established the capital at Xu, Yi said to Qin: "Lord Cao the Pacifier of the East will surely be able to restore and aid the Central Realm; I know where to go!
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao welcomed the emperor to Xu, Zhao Yi told Fan Qin, "The Lord Pacifier of the East will surely restore the realm—I know where our path lies!"

sentences.zh: 」遂還詣操，操以儼為朗陵長。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he returned and presented himself to Cao Cao; Cao appointed Yi as Magistrate of Langling.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to Cao Cao, who made Zhao Yi magistrate of Langling.

sentences.zh: 陽安都尉江夏李通妻伯父犯法，儼收治，致之大辟。

translations.literal: The wife's uncle of Li Tong of Jiangxia, Commandant of Yang'an, violated the law; Yi took him into custody and submitted him to capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The uncle of Li Tong of Jiangxia's wife—Li Tong being commandant of Yang'an—broke the law. Zhao Yi arrested him and sent the case to capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 時殺生之柄，決於牧守，通妻子號泣以請其命。

translations.literal: At that time the power over life and death rested with the prefects and governors; Tong's wife and children wept and wailed to beg for his life.
translations.idiomatic: In those days governors held the power of life and death. Li Tong's wife and children wept and begged for the man's life.

sentences.zh: 通曰：「方與曹公戮力，義不以私廢公！

translations.literal: Tong said: "I am just now joining strength with Lord Cao; by righteousness I cannot let private ties abolish the public cause!
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong said, "I am fighting alongside Lord Cao; duty does not permit private ties to override the public good!"

sentences.zh: 」嘉儼執憲不阿，與為親交。

translations.literal: " He praised Yi for upholding the law without bending and became his close friend.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Zhao Yi for enforcing the law without favor and became his close friend.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，曹操還許。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, Cao Cao returned to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Cao Cao returned to Xu.

sentences.zh: 三月，將復擊張繡。

translations.literal: In the third month, he was about to attack Zhang Xiu again.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he prepared to attack Zhang Xiu again.

sentences.zh: 荀攸曰：「繡與劉表相恃為強；

translations.literal: Xun You said: "Xiu and Liu Biao rely on each other and are thereby strong;
translations.idiomatic: Xun You said, "Zhang Xiu and Liu Biao strengthen each other by mutual reliance;

sentences.zh: 然繡以遊軍仰食於表，表不能供也，勢必乖離。

translations.literal: yet Xiu, as a roving army, looks to Biao for food, and Biao cannot supply him; the situation will surely split apart.
translations.idiomatic: but Zhang Xiu's mobile force depends on Liu Biao for provisions, and Biao cannot sustain it—they must sooner or later part ways.

sentences.zh: 不如緩軍以待之，可誘而致也；

translations.literal: It is better to slacken the army and wait for this; they can be lured and brought in;
translations.idiomatic: Better slacken the advance and wait—we can lure them in;

sentences.zh: 若急之，其勢必相救。

translations.literal: if you press them urgently, they will surely rescue each other.
translations.idiomatic: if we press them hard, they will certainly unite to resist."

sentences.zh: 」操不從，圍繡於穰。

translations.literal: " Cao did not follow this, and besieged Xiu at Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao refused and besieged Zhang Xiu at Rang.

sentences.zh: 2夏，四月，使謁者僕射裴茂詔關中諸將段煨等討李傕，夷其三族。

translations.literal: 2 In summer, the fourth month, he sent Supervisor of Attendants Pei Mao with an edict ordering the Guanzhong generals Duan Hui and others to attack Li Jue and exterminate his three clans.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, he dispatched Pei Mao, Supervisor of Attendants, with an edict for the Guanzhong generals Duan Hui and others to attack Li Jue and exterminate his clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 以煨為安南將軍，封閺鄉侯。

translations.literal: He appointed Hui as General Who Pacifies the South and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hui was made General Who Pacifies the South and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yanxiang.

sentences.zh: 3初，袁紹每得詔書，患其有不便於己者，欲移天子自近，使說曹操以許下埤濕，雒陽殘破，宜徙都鄄城以就全實；

translations.literal: 3 At the beginning, whenever Yuan Shao received an imperial edict, he worried that something in it was inconvenient for himself; he wished to move the Son of Heaven near himself and had someone persuade Cao Cao that Xu's low ground was damp, Luoyang was ruined and broken, and the capital ought to be moved to Juancheng to secure full substance;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, whenever Yuan Shao received an imperial edict he worried it might work against him. He wished to bring the emperor close and had someone urge Cao Cao that Xu was low and damp, Luoyang in ruins—that the capital should be moved to Juancheng for greater security.

sentences.zh: 操拒之。

translations.literal: Cao refused.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao refused.

sentences.zh: 田豐說紹曰：「徙都之計，既不克從，宜早圖許，奉迎天子，動托詔書，號令海內，此算之上者。

translations.literal: Tian Feng urged Shao, saying: "The plan to move the capital having failed to win assent, you ought early to scheme for Xu, welcome the Son of Heaven, and with every move rest on edicts to command the realm within the seas—this is the highest stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Feng urged Yuan Shao, "Since moving the capital failed, you should seize Xu early, welcome the emperor, and rule the empire through imperial edicts—that is the supreme stratagem.

sentences.zh: 不爾，終為人所禽，雖悔無益也。

translations.literal: If not, in the end you will be taken by others; though you repent it will be of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you will end up someone's captive, and regret will avail you nothing."

sentences.zh: 」紹不從。

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 會紹亡卒詣操，云田豐勸紹襲許，操解穰圍而還，張繡率眾追之。

translations.literal: It happened that a deserter from Shao came to Cao and said Tian Feng had urged Shao to strike Xu; Cao lifted the siege of Rang and returned, and Zhang Xiu led his masses in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: A deserter from Yuan Shao's ranks reached Cao Cao with word that Tian Feng had urged a strike on Xu. Cao lifted the siege of Rang and withdrew; Zhang Xiu led his army in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 五月，劉表遣兵救繡，屯於安眾，守險以絕軍後。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Liu Biao sent troops to rescue Xiu; they encamped at Anzhong and held perilous ground to cut off the army's rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Liu Biao sent troops to rescue Zhang Xiu. They encamped at Anzhong, holding the passes to cut off Cao's retreat.

sentences.zh: 操與荀彧書曰：「吾到安眾，破繡必矣。

translations.literal: Cao wrote to Xun Yu: "When I reach Anzhong, I shall surely break Xiu."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wrote to Xun Yu, "When I reach Anzhong, Zhang Xiu is as good as beaten."

sentences.zh: 」及到安眾，操軍前後受敵，操乃夜鑿險偽遁。

translations.literal: When he reached Anzhong, Cao's army was attacked before and behind; Cao thereupon by night cut through difficult ground and feigned flight.
translations.idiomatic: At Anzhong his army was caught between two fires. That night he cut through difficult ground and feigned a retreat.

sentences.zh: 表、繡悉軍來追，操縱奇兵步騎夾攻，大破之，它日，彧問操：「前策賊必破，何也？

translations.literal: Biao and Xiu sent all their armies in pursuit; Cao loosed odd troops of foot and horse to attack from both sides and routed them thoroughly. Another day Yu asked Cao: "Earlier you planned that the bandits would surely be broken—why?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu threw their full strength into the pursuit. Cao Cao threw ambush troops against them from both flanks and won a great victory. Later Xun Yu asked, "You foretold victory—how did you know?"

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「虜遏吾歸師，而與吾死地，吾是以知勝矣。

translations.literal: " Cao said: "The enemy blocked my returning army and thereby gave me a death-ground; for that reason I knew I would win."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "They blocked my retreat and trapped me in death ground—that is why I knew we would win."

sentences.zh: 繡之追操也，賈詡止之曰：「不可追也，追必敗。

translations.literal: When Xiu pursued Cao, Jia Xu stopped him, saying: "You must not pursue; if you pursue you will surely be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Xiu pursued Cao Cao, Jia Xu warned him, "Do not pursue—you will be defeated."

sentences.zh: 」繡不聽，進兵交戰，大敗而還。

translations.literal: " Xiu did not listen; he advanced to battle and returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu ignored him, gave battle, and was routed.

sentences.zh: 詡登城謂繡曰：「促更追之，更戰必勝。

translations.literal: Xu mounted the wall and said to Xiu: "Hurry and pursue again; in another battle you will surely win."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu climbed the wall and called, "Pursue again at once—fight again and you will win."

sentences.zh: 」繡謝曰：「不用公言，以至於此，今已敗，奈何復追？

translations.literal: " Xiu apologized, saying: "I did not use your words and came to this; now we are already defeated—how can we pursue again?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu said, "I ignored your counsel and came to this pass. We are already beaten—how can we pursue again?"

sentences.zh: 」詡曰：「兵勢有變，促追之。

translations.literal: " Xu said: "The military situation has changed; hurry and pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu said, "The situation has shifted—pursue at once."

sentences.zh: 」繡素信詡言，遂收散卒更追，合戰，果以勝還，乃問詡曰：「繡以精兵追退軍，而公曰必敗；

translations.literal: " Xiu had long trusted Xu's words; he thereupon gathered scattered soldiers and pursued again; joining battle, he indeed returned victorious. He then asked Xu: "Xiu with elite troops pursued a retreating army, yet you said we would surely lose;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu had long trusted Jia Xu; he gathered his scattered troops and pursued again. In the encounter he won. He then asked, "I pursued a retreating army with elite troops, and you said we would lose;

sentences.zh: 以敗卒擊勝兵，而公曰必克，悉如公言，何也？

translations.literal: with defeated soldiers striking victorious troops, yet you said we would surely overcome—all was as you said—why?"
translations.idiomatic: then led beaten men against a victorious army, and you said we would win—everything came to pass as you said. How?"

sentences.zh: 」詡曰：「此易知耳。

translations.literal: " Xu said: "This is easy to know."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu said, "That is easy to explain."

sentences.zh: 將軍雖善用兵，非曹公敵也。

translations.literal: Though the general is skilled in using troops, you are not Cao Cao's match.
translations.idiomatic: You are skilled in war, General, but you are no match for Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 曹公軍新退，必自斷後。

translations.literal: Cao Cao's army having newly retreated, he will surely personally guard the rear.
translations.idiomatic: His army had just withdrawn—he would surely cover the retreat himself.

sentences.zh: 故知必敗。

translations.literal: Therefore I knew you would surely lose.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I knew you would lose.

sentences.zh: 曹公攻將軍，既無失策，力未盡而一朝引退，必國內有故也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao attacked the general without any failed stratagem; his strength not yet spent yet in one morning he withdrew—there must have been trouble within the state.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked you without misstep; to withdraw before his strength was spent, he must have had trouble at home.

sentences.zh: 已破將軍，必輕軍速進，留諸將斷後，諸將雖勇，非將軍敵，故雖用敗兵而戰必勝也。

translations.literal: Having already defeated the general, he will surely lead a light force in rapid advance and leave the various generals to guard the rear; though the generals are brave, they are not the general's match—therefore even using defeated soldiers in battle you would surely win."
translations.idiomatic: Having beaten you once, he would press ahead lightly and leave other generals to hold the rear. Brave as they are, they are not your equal—so even with beaten troops you were bound to win."

sentences.zh: 」繡乃服。

translations.literal: " Xiu thereupon was convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 4呂布復與袁術通，遣其中郎將高順及北地太守雁門張遼攻劉備。

translations.literal: 4 Lü Bu again connected with Yuan Shu, sending his Gentlemen of the Palace Gao Shun and Zhang Liao of Yanmen, Administrator of Beidi, to attack Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu renewed ties with Yuan Shu and sent his palace attendant Gao Shun and Zhang Liao of Yanmen, administrator of Beidi, against Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 曹操遣將軍夏侯惇救之，為順等所敗。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent General Xiahou Dun to rescue him; Dun was defeated by Shun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Dun to the rescue; Shun and the others routed him.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，順等破沛城，虜備妻子，備單身走。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, Shun and the others broke Pei city, captured Bei's wife and children, and Bei fled alone.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, they took Pei, captured Liu Bei's family, and Liu Bei fled alone.

sentences.zh: 曹操欲自擊布，諸將皆曰：「劉表、張繡在後，而遠襲呂布，其危必也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao wished personally to strike Bu; the various generals all said: "Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu are in the rear, yet you would strike Lü Bu from afar—danger is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wished to attack Lü Bu himself. His generals objected: "Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu threaten our rear, and a distant strike on Lü Bu would be desperately risky."

sentences.zh: 」荀攸曰：「表、繡新破，勢不敢動，布驍猛，又恃袁術，若從橫淮、泗間，豪傑必應之。

translations.literal: " Xun You said: "Biao and Xiu have newly been defeated; in situation they dare not move. Bu is fierce and bold and again relies on Yuan Shu; if he ranges athwart between Huai and Si, the bold spirits will surely respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You said, "Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu have just been beaten and dare not stir. Lü Bu is fierce and still leans on Yuan Shu; if he ranges the Huai and Si region, every bold spirit will flock to him.

sentences.zh: 今乘其初叛，眾心未一，往可破也。

translations.literal: Now, while taking advantage of his first defection when hearts are not yet united, if you go you can break him."
translations.idiomatic: Strike now, while his defection is fresh and his followers still divided, and you can break him."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Cao said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 」此行，泰山屯帥臧霸、孫觀、吳敦、尹禮、昌豨等皆附於布。

translations.literal: " On this expedition, Zang Ba, Sun Guan, Wu Dun, Yin Li, Chang Xi, and others—the encampment chiefs of Mount Tai—all attached themselves to Bu.
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign Zang Ba, Sun Guan, Wu Dun, Yin Li, Chang Xi, and other Mount Tai band-chiefs all joined Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 操與劉備遇於梁。

translations.literal: Cao met Liu Bei at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao joined Liu Bei at Liang.

sentences.zh: 進至彭城。

translations.literal: He advanced to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 陳宮謂布：「宜逆擊之，以逸擊勞，無不克也。

translations.literal: Chen Gong said to Bu: "You ought to strike them coming; with ease striking labor, nothing will fail to overcome."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong told Lü Bu, "You should meet them on the march—fresh troops against weary ones, and you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「不如待其來攻，蹙著泗水中。

translations.literal: " Bu said: "Better to wait for them to come attack and drive them into the Si River."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu said, "Better wait until they come—we will drive them into the Si River."

sentences.zh: 」冬，十月，操屠彭城。

translations.literal: " In winter, the tenth month, Cao slaughtered Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Cao Cao sacked Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 廣陵太守陳登率郡兵為操先驅，進至下邳。

translations.literal: Chen Deng, Administrator of Guangling, led the commandery troops as Cao's vanguard and advanced to Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng, administrator of Guangling, led his commandery troops as vanguard and pushed on to Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 布自將屢與操戰，皆大敗，還保城，不敢出。

translations.literal: Bu himself led the army and repeatedly fought Cao; each time he was greatly defeated; he returned to hold the city and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu led his army in repeated battles and was routed each time; he withdrew into the city and dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 操遺布書，為陳禍福。

translations.literal: Cao sent Bu a letter, laying out fortune and calamity for him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent a letter setting out the blessings and perils that awaited him.

sentences.zh: 布懼，欲降。

translations.literal: Bu was afraid and wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was afraid and meant to surrender.

sentences.zh: 陳宮曰：「曹操遠來，勢不能久。

translations.literal: Chen Gong said: "Cao Cao has come from afar; in momentum he cannot long endure."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong said, "Cao Cao has come from far away; he cannot stay long."

sentences.zh: 將軍若以步騎出屯於外，宮將餘眾閉守於內。

translations.literal: If the general leads foot and horse out to encamp outside, Gong will lead the remaining masses to shut and hold inside.
translations.idiomatic: If you take infantry and cavalry to camp outside, I will shut the remainder in the city.

sentences.zh: 若向將軍，宮引兵而攻其背；

translations.literal: If they turn toward the general, Gong leads troops to strike their back;
translations.idiomatic: If they turn on you, I strike their rear;

sentences.zh: 若但攻城，則將軍救於外。

translations.literal: if they merely attack the city, then the general rescues from outside.
translations.idiomatic: if they only besiege the city, you rescue from without.

sentences.zh: 不過旬月，操軍食盡，擊之，可破也。

translations.literal: Within no more than ten days and a month, Cao's army's food will be exhausted; strike them and he can be broken."
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month their provisions will fail; then strike and you can break them."

sentences.zh: 」布然之，欲使宮與高順守城，自將騎斷操糧道。

translations.literal: " Bu approved; he wished to have Gong and Gao Shun guard the city while he himself led cavalry to cut Cao's grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu agreed. He would leave Chen Gong and Gao Shun to hold the city while he led cavalry to sever Cao's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 布妻謂布曰：「宮、順素不和，將軍一出，宮、順必不同心共城守也，如有蹉跌，將軍當於何自立乎？

translations.literal: Bu's wife said to Bu: "Gong and Shun have long been at odds; once the general goes out, Gong and Shun will surely not be of one heart in jointly guarding the city; if there is some stumble, where will the general stand on his own?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's wife said, "Chen Gong and Gao Shun have never been on good terms. Once you leave, they will not guard the city as one. If anything goes wrong, where will you stand?

sentences.zh: 且曹氏待公臺如赤子，獨捨而歸我。

translations.literal: Moreover the Cao clan treats Gongtai like a newborn child, yet he alone left them to return to me.
translations.idiomatic: And the Cao family has treated Gongtai like a son—yet he deserted them for you.

sentences.zh: 今將軍厚公臺不過曹氏，而欲委全城，捐妻子，孤軍遠出，若一旦有變，妾豈得復為將軍妻哉！

translations.literal: Now the general's generosity to Gongtai does not exceed the Cao clan's, yet you wish to entrust the whole city, abandon wife and children, and go out alone with a distant army—if suddenly there is change, how can your handmaid again be the general's wife!
translations.idiomatic: You treat Gongtai no better than the Caos did, yet you would entrust the whole city, leave wife and children behind, and ride out alone. If fortune turns, shall I ever be your wife again?"

sentences.zh: 」布乃止，潛遣其官屬許汜、王楷求救於袁術。

translations.literal: " Bu thereupon stopped and secretly sent his officials Xu Si and Wang Kai to beg rescue from Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu held back and secretly sent Xu Si and Wang Kai to Yuan Shu for aid.

sentences.zh: 術曰：「布不與我女，理自當敗，何為復來？

translations.literal: Shu said: "Bu would not give me his daughter—in reason he ought to lose; why come again?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu said, "Lü Bu refused me his daughter—he deserves to lose. Why should he come back to me?"

sentences.zh: 」汜、楷曰：「明上今不救布，為自敗耳。

translations.literal: " Si and Kai said: "If the enlightened lord does not now rescue Bu, it is defeating yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Si and Wang Kai said, "If you do not save Lü Bu now, you defeat yourself."

sentences.zh: 布破，明上亦破也。

translations.literal: When Bu is broken, the enlightened lord is also broken.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Bu falls, you fall with him."

sentences.zh: 」術乃嚴兵為布作聲援。

translations.literal: " Shu thereupon arrayed troops sternly to make a show of support for Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu thereupon mobilized troops to make a show of support.

sentences.zh: 布恐術為女至，故不遣救兵，以綿纏女身縛著馬上，夜自送女出，與操守兵相觸，格射不得過，復還城。

translations.literal: Bu feared that Shu came for the daughter, so he did not send rescue troops; he wrapped the daughter's body in cotton and bound her on a horse, and by night personally sent the daughter out; they clashed with Cao's guarding troops, blocked and shot and could not pass, and returned to the city again.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu feared Yuan Shu wanted only the marriage, so he sent no troops—only bound his daughter in cotton, lashed her to a horse, and tried by night to deliver her to Yuan Shu. They ran into Cao's pickets, could not break through under arrow-fire, and returned to the city.

sentences.zh: 河內太守張楊素與布善，欲救之，不能，乃出兵東市，遙為之勢。

translations.literal: Zhang Yang, Administrator of Henei, had long been friendly with Bu and wished to rescue him but could not; he thereupon sent troops to the eastern market to make a distant show of force for him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang of Henei, who had long been Lü Bu's friend, wished to rescue him but could not; he marched to the eastern market to make a distant demonstration.

sentences.zh: 十一月，楊將楊醜殺楊以應操，別將眭固復殺醜，將其眾北合袁紹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yang's officer Yang Chou killed Yang to respond to Cao; the separate officer Sui Gu again killed Chou and led his masses north to join Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yang Chou, a subordinate of Zhang Yang, killed his master to please Cao Cao; another officer, Sui Gu, killed Chou in turn and led the troops north to join Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 楊性仁和，無威刑，下人謀反發覺，對之涕泣，輒原不問，故及於難。

translations.literal: Yang's nature was benevolent and mild; he had no awe-inspiring punishments; when subordinates' rebellious plots were discovered, he wept facing them and invariably pardoned without inquiry—therefore he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang was gentle by nature and enforced no stern discipline. When plots were uncovered he wept before the conspirators and always pardoned them—thus his end.

sentences.zh: 操掘塹圍下邳，積久，士卒疲敝，欲還，荀攸、郭嘉曰：「呂布勇而無謀，今屢戰皆北，銳氣衰矣。

translations.literal: Cao dug trenches and besieged Xiapi; as it dragged on, soldiers and officers were weary and worn; he wished to return. Xun You and Guo Jia said: "Lü Bu is brave but without stratagem; now he has fought repeatedly and each time gone north—the keen edge of spirit has declined.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao dug trenches around Xiapi. The siege wore on; his men grew exhausted and he thought of withdrawing. Xun You and Guo Jia said, "Lü Bu is brave but lacks counsel. He has lost battle after battle; his spirit is broken.

sentences.zh: 三軍以將為主，主衰則軍無奮意。

translations.literal: The three armies take the commander as their master; when the master declines, the armies have no mind to strive.
translations.idiomatic: An army follows its leader's spirit—a broken leader leaves men unwilling to fight.

sentences.zh: 陳宮有智而遲。

translations.literal: Chen Gong has wisdom but is slow.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong is clever but slow.

sentences.zh: 今及布氣之未復，宮謀之未定，急攻之，布可拔也。

translations.literal: Now, while catching Bu before his spirit has recovered and Gong before his plans are settled, attack urgently and Bu can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Press the attack before Lü Bu rallies and Chen Gong settles on a plan, and Lü Bu can be taken."

sentences.zh: 」乃引沂、泗灌城。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they led the Yi and Si to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: They diverted the Yi and Si rivers to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 月餘，布益困迫，臨城謂操軍士曰：「卿曹無相困，我當自首於明公。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Bu grew ever more distressed and pressed; facing the city he said to Cao's soldiers: "You gentlemen, do not press me hard; I shall surrender myself to the enlightened lord."
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Lü Bu was desperate. From the wall he called to Cao's men, "Stop pressing me—I will surrender to your lord."

sentences.zh: 」陳宮曰：「逆賊曹操，何等明公！

translations.literal: Chen Gong said: "The rebel traitor Cao Cao—what sort of enlightened lord is that!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong said, "Cao Cao the traitor—what sort of 'lord' is he?

sentences.zh: 今日降之，若卵投石，豈可得全也！

translations.literal: To surrender to him today is like an egg cast against stone—how could you attain preservation!"
translations.idiomatic: Surrender today and you are an egg against stone—how could you survive?"

sentences.zh: 布將侯成亡其名馬，已而復得之，諸將合禮以賀成，成分酒肉先入獻布。

translations.literal: Bu's general Hou Cheng lost his famous horse, then afterward recovered it; the various generals together with propriety congratulated Cheng; Cheng divided wine and meat and first entered to present them to Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's general Hou Cheng lost a celebrated horse and later recovered it. His comrades gathered to congratulate him; Hou Cheng set out meat and wine and brought the first portion to Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 布怒曰：「布禁酒而卿等醞釀，為欲因酒共謀布邪？

translations.literal: Bu angrily said: "Bu forbids wine, yet you gentlemen brew liquor—is it that you wish by wine to plot against Bu together?!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu raged, "I forbid wine, and you brew it—do you mean to plot against me over the cup?"

sentences.zh: 」成忿懼，十二月，癸酉，成與諸將宋憲、魏續等共執陳宮、高順，率其眾降。

translations.literal: " Cheng, resentful and afraid—in the twelfth month, on guiyou, Cheng with the generals Song Xian, Wei Xu, and others jointly seized Chen Gong and Gao Shun and led their masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Cheng, furious and afraid, did so. On guiyou of the twelfth month he joined Song Xian, Wei Xu, and others in seizing Chen Gong and Gao Shun and leading their men in surrender.

sentences.zh: 布與麾下登白門樓。

translations.literal: Bu and his followers beneath him ascended White Gate Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu climbed White Gate Tower with his followers.

sentences.zh: 兵圍之急，布令左右取其首詣操，左右不忍，乃下降。

translations.literal: The army pressed the siege urgently; Bu ordered those at his sides to take his head and present it to Cao; those at his sides could not bear to, and thereupon descended in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The siege tightened. Lü Bu ordered his men to take his head to Cao Cao; they could not bear to, and instead went down to surrender.

sentences.zh: 布見操曰：「今日已往，天下定矣。

translations.literal: Bu saw Cao and said: "From today what is past is past—the realm is settled."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu faced Cao Cao and said, "The past is done—from this day the realm is settled."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「何以言之？

translations.literal: " Cao said: "By what do you say this?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「明公之所患不過於布，今已服矣。

translations.literal: " Bu said: "What the enlightened lord worries about is nothing beyond Bu; now I have submitted."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu said, "Your worst enemy was no more than I—and I have submitted."

sentences.zh: 若令布將騎，明公將步，天下不足定也。

translations.literal: If you order Bu to lead horse and you lead foot soldiers, the realm is not insufficient to settle.
translations.idiomatic: Give me the cavalry, you keep the infantry, and the realm is yours."

sentences.zh: 」顧謂劉備曰：「玄德，卿為坐上客，我為降虜，繩縛我急，獨不可一言邪？

translations.literal: " He turned and said to Liu Bei: "Xuan De, you are the honored guest at the seat; I am the captive taken in surrender; they bind me tight with ropes—is it that you alone cannot speak a word?"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Liu Bei: "Xuande, you are the honored guest and I the bound captive—they truss me tight. Will you not speak for me?"

sentences.zh: 」操笑曰：「縛虎不得不急。

translations.literal: " Cao laughed and said: "Binding a tiger—you cannot but be urgent."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed. "When you bind a tiger, you bind tight."

sentences.zh: 」乃命緩布縛。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Lü Bu's bonds loosened.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the bonds loosened.

sentences.zh: 劉備曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Liu Bei said: "It cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei said, "You must not."

sentences.zh: 明公不見呂布事丁建陽、董太師乎！

translations.literal: My lord, have you not seen how Lü Bu served Ding Jianyang and Grand Tutor Dong!
translations.idiomatic: My lord, have you forgotten what Lü Bu did to Ding Jianyang and Grand Tutor Dong!

sentences.zh: 」操頷之。

translations.literal: " Cao nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 布目備曰：「大耳兒，最叵信！

translations.literal: Bu glared at Bei and said: "Big-Ears—you are the least trustworthy of all!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu glared at Liu Bei and said, "Big-Ears—you are the most faithless man alive!

sentences.zh: 操謂陳宮曰：「公台平生自謂智有餘，今竟何如？

translations.literal: Cao said to Chen Gong: "Gongtai, you always claimed your wisdom was more than enough—how does it stand now?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said to Chen Gong, "Gongtai, you always boasted that your wits were more than sufficient—how do matters stand now?

sentences.zh: 」宮指布曰：「是子不用宮言，以至於此。

translations.literal: " Gong pointed at Bu and said: "This fellow would not heed Gong's words, and so has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong pointed at Lü Bu and said, "This man refused to heed my counsel, and so has come to this pass.

sentences.zh: 若其見從，亦未必為禽也。

translations.literal: Had he followed my advice, he might not necessarily have been taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Had he listened, he might never have been captured at all.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「奈卿老母何？

translations.literal: " Cao said: "What of your aged mother?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked, "What of your aged mother?

sentences.zh: 」宮曰：「宮聞以孝治天下者不害人之親。

translations.literal: " Gong said: "Gong has heard that one who governs all under Heaven by filial piety does not harm another's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong replied, "I have heard that a ruler who governs the realm through filial piety does not harm another man's family.

sentences.zh: 老母存否，在明公，不在宮也。

translations.literal: Whether my mother lives or dies rests with my lord, not with Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Whether my mother lives or dies is for you to decide, not for me.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「奈卿妻子何？

translations.literal: " Cao said: "What of your wife and children?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked, "What of your wife and children?

sentences.zh: 」宮曰：「宮聞施仁政於天下者不絕人之祀，妻子存否，在明公，不在宮也。

translations.literal: " Gong said: "Gong has heard that one who extends benevolent government to all under Heaven does not cut off another's sacrifices; whether wife and children live or die rests with my lord, not with Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong said, "I have heard that a ruler who extends benevolent government across the realm does not extinguish another's line. Whether my wife and children live or die is for you to decide, not for me.

sentences.zh: 」操未復言。
