translations.literal: " Cao spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 宮請就刑，遂出，不顧，操為之泣涕，并布、順皆縊殺之，傳首許市。

translations.literal: Gong asked to go to execution; he went out and did not look back. Cao wept for him. Both Bu and Shun were strangled to death, and their heads were displayed in the markets of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong asked to face execution, walked out without a backward glance, and Cao Cao wept for him. Lü Bu and Gao Shun were both strangled, and their heads were sent to the markets of Xu for public display.

sentences.zh: 操召陳宮之母，養之終其身，嫁宮女，撫視其家，皆厚於初。

translations.literal: Cao summoned Chen Gong's mother, supported her to the end of her life, married off Gong's daughter, and cared for his household—all with greater generosity than before.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao summoned Chen Gong's mother and provided for her until her death; he gave Gong's daughter in marriage and looked after his household—all with greater generosity than before.

sentences.zh: 前尚書令陳紀、紀子群在布軍中，操皆禮而用之。

translations.literal: The former Director of the Secretariat Chen Ji and Ji's son Qun were in Bu's army; Cao treated them with courtesy and employed them.
translations.idiomatic: The former Director of the Secretariat Chen Ji and his son Chen Qun had been in Lü Bu's camp; Cao Cao received them with courtesy and put them to use.

sentences.zh: 張遼將其眾降，拜中郎將。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao led his followers in surrender and was appointed Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao surrendered with his troops and was appointed Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 臧霸自亡匿，操募索得之，使霸招吳敦、尹禮、孔觀等，皆詣操降。

translations.literal: Zang Ba had fled into hiding; Cao recruited and sought him out, then had Ba summon Wu Dun, Yin Li, Kong Guan, and the rest, and all came to Cao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba had gone into hiding; Cao Cao hunted him down, then had him summon Wu Dun, Yin Li, Kong Guan, and the others, and all came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 操乃分琅邪、東海為城陽、利城、昌慮郡，悉以霸等為守、相。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon divided Langye and Donghai into the commanderies of Chengyang, Licheng, and Changlu, and appointed Ba and the others as administrators and chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then carved Langye and Donghai into the commanderies of Chengyang, Licheng, and Changlu, and installed Zang Ba and his fellows as administrators and chancellors.

sentences.zh: 初，操在兗州，以徐翕、毛暉為將。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Cao was in Yan Province, he had made Xu Xi and Mao Hui his generals.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cao Cao held Yan Province, he had appointed Xu Xi and Mao Hui as his generals.

sentences.zh: 及兗州亂，翕、暉皆叛。

translations.literal: When Yan Province fell into turmoil, Xi and Hui both rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Province erupted in rebellion, both men had turned against him.

sentences.zh: 兗州既定，翕、暉亡命投霸。

translations.literal: Once Yan Province was settled, Xi and Hui fled as outlaws and threw themselves on Ba's protection.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Province was pacified, Xu Xi and Mao Hui fled as outlaws and sought refuge with Zang Ba.

sentences.zh: 操語劉備，令霸送二首，霸謂備曰：「霸所以能自立者，以不為此也。

translations.literal: Cao spoke to Liu Bei and ordered Ba to deliver the two men's heads. Ba said to Bei: "The reason Ba could stand on his own was that he would not do this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao spoke to Liu Bei and ordered Zang Ba to deliver the two men's heads. Zang Ba told Liu Bei, "The reason I could hold my own was that I would never do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 霸受主公生全之恩，不敢違命。

translations.literal: Ba received my lord's grace in sparing his life and dares not disobey the command.
translations.idiomatic: Your lord spared my life, and I dare not disobey your command.

sentences.zh: 然王霸之君，可以義告，願將軍為之辭。

translations.literal: Yet a hegemon may be addressed through righteousness; I beg the General to plead on my behalf.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, General, to plead my case for me.

sentences.zh: 」備以霸言白操，操嘆息謂霸曰：「此古人之事，而君能行之，孤之願也。

translations.literal: " Bei reported Ba's words to Cao; Cao sighed and said to Ba: "This is the conduct of the ancients, yet you can perform it—this is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei relayed Zang Ba's words to Cao Cao, who sighed and said to Zang Ba, "Such conduct belongs to the ancients, yet you live it—this is exactly what I hoped for.

sentences.zh: 」皆以翕、暉為郡守。

translations.literal: " Both Xi and Hui were made commandery administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xi and Mao Hui were both appointed commandery administrators.

sentences.zh: 陳登以功加伏波將軍。

translations.literal: Chen Deng was promoted to General Who Subdues the Waves for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements, Chen Deng was promoted to General Who Subdues the Waves.

sentences.zh: 5劉表與袁紹深相結約。

translations.literal: 5 Liu Biao and Yuan Shao were deeply bound in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao and Yuan Shao were bound in a deep alliance.

sentences.zh: 治中鄧羲諫表，表曰：「內不失貢職，外不背盟主，此天下之達義也。

translations.literal: Director of Retainers Deng Xi remonstrated with Biao; Biao said: "Within, one does not fail in tribute and office; without, one does not betray one's ally—this is the great principle under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Retainers Deng Xi remonstrated with Liu Biao, who replied, "Within, I fulfill my duties to the court; without, I honor my alliance—this is the supreme principle of the realm.

sentences.zh: 治中獨何怪乎？

translations.literal: Why does the Director alone find it strange?
translations.idiomatic: Why does the Director alone find that strange?

sentences.zh: 」羲乃辭疾而退。

translations.literal: " Xi thereupon pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xi thereupon pleaded illness and withdrew from office.

sentences.zh: 長沙太守張羨，性屈強，表不禮焉。

translations.literal: Administrator of Changsha Zhang Xian was by nature obstinate and unyielding; Biao did not treat him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian, Administrator of Changsha, was obstinate and unyielding by nature, and Liu Biao showed him no courtesy.

sentences.zh: 郡人桓階說羨舉長沙、零陵、桂陽三郡以拒表，遣使附於曹操，羨從之。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Huan Jie, persuaded Xian to raise Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang—three commanderies—to resist Biao, and sent envoys to attach himself to Cao Cao; Xian followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jie, a man of the commandery, persuaded Zhang Xian to rally Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang in resistance to Liu Biao and to send envoys offering allegiance to Cao Cao; Zhang Xian agreed.

sentences.zh: 6孫策遣其正議校尉張紘獻方物，曹操欲撫納之，表策為討逆將軍，封吳侯；

translations.literal: 6 Sun Ce sent his Standard-Bearer for Correct Discourse Zhang Hong to present local products; Cao Cao wished to win him over and memorialized to appoint Ce General Who Punishes the Rebellious and enfeoff him as Marquis of Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent his Standard-Bearer for Correct Discourse Zhang Hong to present tribute. Cao Cao meant to win him over and memorialized to appoint Sun Ce General Who Punishes Rebellion and enfeoff him as Marquis of Wu;

sentences.zh: 以弟女配策弟匡，又為子彰取孫賁女；

translations.literal: he gave his younger brother's daughter in marriage to Ce's younger brother Kuang, and for his son Zhang took the daughter of Sun Ben;
translations.idiomatic: he gave his younger brother's daughter in marriage to Sun Ce's brother Sun Kuang, and for his son Cao Zhang took the daughter of Sun Ben;

sentences.zh: 禮辟策弟權、翊；

translations.literal: he courteously summoned Ce's younger brothers Quan and Yi;
translations.idiomatic: he courteously summoned Sun Ce's younger brothers Sun Quan and Sun Yi;

sentences.zh: 以張紘為侍御史。

translations.literal: and he appointed Zhang Hong Attending Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: and he appointed Zhang Hong Attending Secretary.

sentences.zh: 袁術以周瑜為居巢長，以臨淮魯肅為東城長。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu made Zhou Yu magistrate of Juchao and Lu Su of Linhuai magistrate of Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu appointed Zhou Yu magistrate of Juchao and Lu Su of Linhuai magistrate of Dongcheng.

sentences.zh: 瑜、肅知術終無所成，皆棄官渡江從孫策。

translations.literal: Yu and Su knew that Shu would accomplish nothing in the end; both abandoned their posts, crossed the river, and followed Sun Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu and Lu Su saw that Yuan Shu would come to nothing; both abandoned their posts, crossed the Yangtze, and joined Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 策以瑜為建威中郎將。

translations.literal: Ce made Yu Establishing Might Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce appointed Zhou Yu Establishing Might Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 肅因家於曲阿。

translations.literal: Su thereupon made his home at Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su settled his household at Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 曹操表徵王朗，策遣朗還。

translations.literal: Cao Cao memorialized to summon Wang Lang; Ce sent Lang back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao memorialized to summon Wang Lang; Sun Ce sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 操以朗為諫議大夫，參司空軍事。

translations.literal: Cao made Lang Remonstrance and Policy Grandee and staff officer on the Minister of Works' military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao appointed Wang Lang Remonstrance and Policy Grandee and attached him to the Minister of Works' military staff.

sentences.zh: 袁術遣間使繼印綬與丹陽宗帥祖郎等，使激動山越，共圖孫策。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu sent secret envoys bearing successive seals and ribbons to the clan chieftain of Danyang, Zu Lang, and others, stirring up the Shanyue to join in plotting against Sun Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu sent secret envoys bearing seals and ribbons to Zu Lang, a clan chieftain of Danyang, and others, inciting the Shanyue to join in a plot against Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 劉繇之奔豫章也，太史慈遁於蕪湖山中，自稱丹陽太守。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao fled to Yuzhang, Taishi Ci hid in the mountains of Wuhu and styled himself Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao fled to Yuzhang, Taishi Ci hid in the mountains of Wuhu and styled himself Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 策已定宣城以東，惟涇以西六縣未服，慈因進住涇縣，大為山越所附。

translations.literal: Ce had already secured the lands east of Xuancheng; only the six counties west of Jing remained unsubmissive. Ci advanced and encamped at Jing County, and the Shanyue rallied to him in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had secured everything east of Xuancheng; only six counties west of Jing still held out. Taishi Ci advanced to Jing County and won a vast following among the Shanyue.

sentences.zh: 於是策自將討祖郎於陵陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ce personally led a campaign against Zu Lang at Lingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce then led his army in person against Zu Lang at Lingyang.

sentences.zh: 禽之。

translations.literal: He captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He captured him.

sentences.zh: 策謂郎曰：「爾昔襲孤，斫孤馬鞍，今創軍立事，除棄宿恨，惟取能用，與天下通耳，非但汝，汝勿恐怖。

translations.literal: Ce said to Lang: "You once raided me and hacked my saddle; now, as I build my army and establish my enterprise, I cast off old grudges and take only those who can serve. This holds for all—not for you alone. Do not be afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce told Zu Lang, "You once ambushed me and hacked my saddle to pieces. Now I am building my army and my cause, and I set aside old scores—I take only those who can serve. That goes for everyone, not just you. Have no fear.

sentences.zh: 」郎叩頭謝罪，即破械，署門下賊曹。

translations.literal: " Lang kowtowed in confession of guilt; Ce immediately removed his bonds and appointed him Bandit Suppression Clerk of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Lang kowtowed in confession; Sun Ce immediately removed his bonds and appointed him Bandit Suppression Clerk of the Household.

sentences.zh: 又討太史慈於勇裡，禽之，解縛，捉其手曰：「寧識神亭時邪？

translations.literal: He also campaigned against Taishi Ci at Yongli, captured him, loosed his bonds, took his hand, and said: "Do you remember Shen Village?
translations.idiomatic: He also fought Taishi Ci at Yongli, captured him, cut his bonds, took his hand, and said, "Do you remember Shen Village?

sentences.zh: 若卿爾時得我云何？

translations.literal: If you had taken me then, what would you have done with me?
translations.idiomatic: If you had taken me then, what would you have done with me?

sentences.zh: 」慈曰：「未可量也。

translations.literal: " Ci said: "That cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci replied, "Who can say?

sentences.zh: 」策大笑曰：「今日之事，當與卿共之。

translations.literal: " Ce laughed greatly and said: "Today's affair shall be shared with you.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce laughed and said, "What happens today, we shall share together.

sentences.zh: 聞卿有烈義，天下智士也，但所託未得其人耳。

translations.literal: I have heard that you possess fierce loyalty—you are a wise man under Heaven, but the man you served was not the right one.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard you are a man of fierce loyalty—a wise man under Heaven—but you served the wrong master.

sentences.zh: 孤是卿知己，勿憂不如意也。

translations.literal: I am your confidant; do not worry that things will not go as you wish.
translations.idiomatic: I am your true friend. Do not worry that things will go ill for you.

sentences.zh: 」即署門下督。

translations.literal: " He immediately appointed him Household Controller.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed him Household Controller.

sentences.zh: 軍還，祖郎、太史慈俱在前導，軍人以為榮。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Zu Lang and Taishi Ci both marched in the vanguard, and the soldiers took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home, Zu Lang and Taishi Ci both rode in the vanguard, and the soldiers counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 會劉繇卒於豫章，士眾萬餘人，欲奉豫章太守華歆為主。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Yao died at Yuzhang; more than ten thousand soldiers and followers wished to install Hua Xin, Administrator of Yuzhang, as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liu Yao died at Yuzhang. More than ten thousand of his soldiers and followers wished to install Hua Xin, Administrator of Yuzhang, as their leader.

sentences.zh: 歆以為因時擅命，非人臣所宜，眾守之連月，卒謝遣之。

translations.literal: Xin held that seizing authority in a time of opportunity was not what a subject should do; the masses pressed him for months, and in the end he declined and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin held that seizing command in a moment of crisis was no fit act for a subject. The troops pressed him for months, but in the end he refused and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 其眾未有所附，策命太史慈往撫安之，謂慈曰：「劉牧往責吾為袁氏攻廬江，吾先君兵數千人，盡在公路許，吾志在立事，安得不屈意於公路以求之乎？

translations.literal: His followers had no one to attach to; Ce ordered Taishi Ci to go and pacify them, saying to Ci: "Governor Liu once reproached me for attacking Lü Jiang on Yuan Shu's behalf. My late father's troops, several thousand strong, were all with Gonglu. My aim was to accomplish something—how could I not humble myself before Gonglu to obtain them?
translations.idiomatic: His troops had no leader. Sun Ce ordered Taishi Ci to go and win them over, telling him, "Governor Liu once reproached me for attacking Lü Jiang on Yuan Shu's behalf. My late father's troops, several thousand strong, were all in Yuan Shu's hands. I meant to build something of my own—how could I not humble myself before him to get them back?

sentences.zh: 其後不遵臣節，諫之不從。

translations.literal: Afterward he failed in the duties of a subject, and though I remonstrated, he would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he betrayed every duty of a subject, and when I remonstrated, he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 丈夫義交，苟有大故，不得不離。

translations.literal: When men bond in righteousness, if a great cause arises, parting is unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: When men swear friendship in righteousness, a grave breach leaves no choice but to part.

sentences.zh: 吾交求公路及絕之本末如此，恨不及其生時與共論辯也。

translations.literal: The beginning and end of my dealings with Qiu and my break with him were thus; I regret only that I could not debate it with him while he lived.
translations.idiomatic: That is the full story of my bond with Yuan Shu and my break with him. I regret only that I could not argue it out with him face to face while he lived.

sentences.zh: 今兒子在豫章，卿往視之。

translations.literal: Now his sons are in Yuzhang—go and look in on them.
translations.idiomatic: His sons are in Yuzhang now—go and see to them.

sentences.zh: 並宣孤意於其部曲。

translations.literal: Proclaim my intent also to his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Make my intentions known to his troops as well.

sentences.zh: 部曲樂來者與俱來，不樂來者且安慰之。

translations.literal: Those who wish to come, bring with you; those who do not, comfort them for the present.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to join you may come; those who do not, reassure them where they stand.

sentences.zh: 並觀華子魚所以牧御方規何如。

translations.literal: Observe also what policies Ziyu employs in governing and what plans he holds.
translations.idiomatic: And observe what policies Ziyu pursues and what designs he harbors.

sentences.zh: 卿須幾兵，多少隨意。

translations.literal: How many troops you need—take as many as you wish.
translations.idiomatic: As for troops, take however many you think fit.

sentences.zh: 」慈曰：「慈有不赦之罪，將軍量同桓、文，當盡死以報德。

translations.literal: " Ci said: "Ci bears an unpardonable crime; the General measures me equal to Duke Huan and Duke Wen—I must give my life to repay such grace.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci said, "I bear an unpardonable offense, yet you treat me as Duke Huan and Duke Wen treated their men—I owe you my life.

sentences.zh: 今並息兵，兵不宜多，將數十人足矣。

translations.literal: Now arms are at rest everywhere; troops should not be many—a few dozen men will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is at peace for now; I need no great escort—a few dozen men will do.

sentences.zh: 」左右皆曰：「慈必北去不還。

translations.literal: " Those at his side all said: "Ci will surely go north and never return.
translations.idiomatic: Those around Sun Ce said, "Taishi Ci will go north and never come back.

sentences.zh: 」策曰：「子義捨我，當復從誰！

translations.literal: " Ce said: "If Ziyi leaves me, whom else would he follow!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce said, "If Ziyi leaves me, whom else would he serve?

sentences.zh: 」餞送昌門，把腕別曰：「何時能還？

translations.literal: " At the farewell at Chang Gate, he grasped his wrist in parting and said: "When can you return?
translations.idiomatic: At the farewell at Chang Gate he grasped Taishi Ci's wrist and asked, "When will you return?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「不過六十日。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Not more than sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci answered, "No more than sixty days.

sentences.zh: 」慈行，議者猶紛紜言遣之非計。

translations.literal: " Ci departed; the debaters still clamored that sending him was a mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci set out, yet his critics still insisted that letting him go had been a mistake.

sentences.zh: 策曰：「諸君勿復言，孤斷之詳矣。

translations.literal: Ce said: "Do not speak further, gentlemen—I have judged this thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce said, "Speak no more of it, gentlemen—I have judged this matter thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 太史子義雖氣勇有膽烈，然非縱橫之人，其必秉道義，重然諾，一以意許知己，死亡不相負，諸君勿憂也。

translations.literal: Taishi Ziyi, though spirited, brave, and fierce of heart, is not a man of shifting schemes; he will surely uphold the Way and honor his word. Once he pledges himself to a confidant, he will not fail that pledge even in death. Do not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ziyi is bold and fierce, but he is no schemer. He will keep faith with the Way and honor his word. Once he gives his pledge to a friend, he will not betray it, even at the cost of his life. Have no fear.

sentences.zh: 」慈果如期而反，謂策曰：「華子魚，良德也，然無他方規，自守而已。

translations.literal: " Ci indeed returned on schedule and said to Ce: "Ziyu is a man of fine virtue, yet he has no larger design—he merely holds his ground.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci returned on schedule and reported to Sun Ce, "Ziyu is a man of fine virtue, but he has no larger design—he merely holds his own.

sentences.zh: 又，丹陽僮芝，自擅廬陵，鄱陽民帥別立宗部，言『我已別立郡海昏上繚，不受發召』，子魚但睹視之而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, Tong Zhi of Danyang has seized Luling for himself; a local chief of Poyang has set up a separate clan regiment, declaring, 'I have already established the commandery of Haihun Shangliao and will not answer your summons'—Ziyu only looks on and does nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Tong Zhi of Danyang has seized Luling on his own authority; a local chief of Poyang has set up a separate clan regiment, declaring, 'I have established the commandery of Haihun Shangliao and will not answer your summons'—and Ziyu only watches and does nothing.

sentences.zh: 」策拊掌大笑，遂有兼併之志。

translations.literal: " Ce clapped his hands and laughed greatly, and from that moment harbored designs of annexation.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce clapped his hands and laughed aloud—and from that moment he set his heart on conquest.

sentences.zh: 7袁紹連年攻公孫瓚，不能克，以書諭之，欲相與釋憾連和；

translations.literal: 7 Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan year after year without overcoming him; he sent a letter admonishing him, wishing to release old grievances and join in alliance;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had attacked Gongsun Zan year after year without overcoming him. He sent a letter urging reconciliation and alliance;

sentences.zh: 瓚不答，而增修守備，謂長史太原關靖曰：「當今四方虎爭，無有能坐吾城下相守經年者明矣，袁本初其若我何！

translations.literal: Zan did not reply but instead strengthened his defenses, saying to his Chief Clerk Guan Jing of Taiyuan: "Today the four quarters contend like tigers; clearly none can sit beneath my walls and hold a stalemate for a year—what can Yuan Benchu do to me!
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan did not reply but redoubled his defenses, telling his Chief Clerk Guan Jing of Taiyuan, "The realm is a battlefield of tigers—no one can sit under my walls and grind me down for a year. What can Yuan Benchu do to me!

sentences.zh: 」紹於是大興兵以攻瓚。

translations.literal: " Shao thereupon raised a great army to attack Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao thereupon mobilized a great army against Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 先是瓚別將有為敵所圍者，瓚不救，曰：「救一人，使後將恃救，不肯力戰。

translations.literal: Earlier, when one of Zan's detached generals was surrounded by the enemy, Zan did not rescue him, saying: "If you rescue one man, later generals will rely on rescue and refuse to fight with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when one of Gongsun Zan's detached generals was surrounded, Gongsun Zan refused to rescue him, saying, "Save one man today, and tomorrow every general will count on rescue instead of fighting with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 」及紹來攻，瓚南界別營，自度守則不能自固，又知必不見救，或降或潰。

translations.literal: " When Shao came to attack, Zan's southern-border detached camps, judging that if they held fast they could not secure themselves and knowing they would surely not be rescued, either surrendered or fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao attacked, Gongsun Zan's detached camps along the southern border saw that they could not hold and knew rescue would never come; they surrendered or fled.

sentences.zh: 紹軍徑至其門，瓚遣子續請救於黑山諸帥，而欲自將突騎出傍西山，擁黑山之眾侵掠冀州，橫斷紹後。

translations.literal: Shao's army reached his gates directly; Zan sent his son Xu to beg rescue from the chieftains of the Black Mountains, while he himself intended to lead his shock cavalry out along the western hills, gather the Black Mountain masses, raid Ji Province, and cut Shao's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's army marched straight to his gates. Gongsun Zan sent his son Gongsun Xu to beg aid from the Black Mountain chieftains while he himself planned to lead his shock cavalry out along the western hills, rally the Black Mountain bands, raid Ji Province, and sever Yuan Shao's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 關靖諫曰：「今將軍將士莫不懷瓦解之心，所以猶能相守者，顧戀其居處老小，而恃將軍為主故耳。

translations.literal: Guan Jing remonstrated, saying: "Now the General's officers and soldiers all harbor hearts ready to dissolve; the reason they can still hold together is that they cherish their homes and their young, and rely on the General as their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Jing remonstrated, saying, "Your officers and soldiers are ready to fall apart. The only reason they still stand together is love for their homes and families—and faith in you as their lord.

sentences.zh: 堅守曠日，或可使紹自退。

translations.literal: If we hold firm for many days, we may yet make Shuo withdraw of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold out for a long siege, Yuan Shao may yet withdraw on his own.

sentences.zh: 若捨之而出，後無鎮重，易京之危，可立待也。

translations.literal: If you abandon this place and go out, afterward there will be nothing to anchor the realm; the peril of Yijing can be awaited at once.
translations.idiomatic: If you leave the fortress, you will lose your base; the disaster of Yijing will come at once.

sentences.zh: 」瓚乃止。

translations.literal: Zan thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 紹漸相攻逼，瓚眾日蹙。

translations.literal: Shuo gradually pressed the attack; Zan's forces grew daily more cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao pressed the siege; Gongsun Zan's position grew tighter by the day.
